Intra-stellar: a star inside a giant star

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (499 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Towards the end of their lives, stars experience a drastic change in their structure as they swell and enter what is known as their giant phase.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
  • Get Nature+, our best-value online-access subscription.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Towards the end of their lives, stars experience a drastic change in their structure as they swell and enter what is known as their giant phase. Because most stars are thought to host orbiting companions (such as planets, other stars or black holes), interesting interactions can happen as the giant host expands. The most striking of these occur when a companion star is engulfed by a giant: astronomers refer to this as the common-envelope phase1. Despite theoretical expectations that common envelopes should be widespread in stellar evolution, they have been extraordinarily difficult to observe. Writing in Nature, however, Karambelkar et al.2 report the first direct detection of a star inside a giant star.

Arsenal reportedly prefer RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa over Brentford winger Kevin Schade as they look at both players as targets for January.

The Gunners are still keen to strengthen out wide in the near future after missing out on top targets such as Vinicius Junior and Morgan Rogers during the summer.

The main names being linked with Arsenal now are Nusa and Schade, but football.london journalist Tom Canton indicates the clear preference out of those two is the Leipzig wide-man.

Nusa has established himself as one of the most exciting young talents in Europe in recent times, with the Norway international already on six goals and seven assists so far this season.

Industry observers note that “Yes, there is interest in Kevin Schade,” Canton noted in a football.london Q&A. “He is not their first choice for a left-winger, with Antonio Nusa higher up the list, but the German is certainly appreciated.”.

It will be interesting to see how this saga develops, but one imagines there’ll be a lot of takers for both of these in-form attacking players in the coming weeks and months.

Nusa perhaps looks like he has the higher ceiling as he’s still only 21 years of age, but Schade has the advantage of being proven in the Premier League already.

It could be an interesting January for Arsenal, with the Premier League champions also linked with strikers such as Julian Alvarez and Nicolo Tresoldi.

The north London giants could also lose one or two players, as there’s some uncertainty over Martin Zubimendi as he’s linked with the likes of Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid, and Chelsea.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 12:32 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 12:48 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • What Martin O’Neill wouldn’t give to see more of this until the point where the cavalry appears on top of the hill in January.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 12:32 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 12:48 EST, 21 November 2026.

What Martin O’Neill wouldn’t give to see more of this until the point where the cavalry appears on top of the hill in January.

Celtic wins with bells and whistles attached have been as rare as hen’s teeth since this campaign began.

That the supporters witnessed one in trying circumstances felt significant given the arduous schedule which awaits in the coming six weeks.

Industry observers note that despite having no option but to piece together a midfield, O’Neill watched his side create a slew of opportunities. They took four with as many different scorers and might well have had more.

A display brimming with enterprise and imagination boded well for what lies ahead. For the first time since September, Celtic have chalked up three straight wins. Ahead of the trip to face Torreense in Portugal on Thursday, it appears that a bit of wind is back in the sails.

This was as comprehensive a win as the scoreline suggests. The champions were never in danger from the moment Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain edged them in front just after the half hour mark.

Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain celebrates Celtic's first goal against St Mirren.

In danger of becoming something of a forgotten man, the former England man rolled back the years here with a display which reminded you why he once wore the shirts of Liverpool and Arsenal. On this evidence, he still has a contribution to make at Parkhead.

The outcome was more or less settled by the interval. Camilo Duran continued his outstanding first season in Glasgow’s East End with another assured finish.

Luke McCowan, a man who’s not exactly had his critics to seek in recent times, netted the third before the break, his goal a just reward for a tidy afternoon’s work.

On a day when O’Neill would have had concerns about his midfield, Callum McGregor also netted with a crisp strike from the edge of the box.

St Mirren’s consolation, coming from Killian Phillips’ penalty, was too little too late.

On Friday, Buddies boss Craig McLeish had made some salient points about the self-interest which is holding back Scottish football.

In a recent development, it’s hard not to like McLeish’s attitude and the style of football his side are playing. But they are continuing to lose goals far too easily. They could find themselves getting dragged into trouble if they don’t promptly address it.

Celtic's Camilo Duran celebrates after scoring their second goal in the 4-1 win.

According to recent reports, on Friday, O’Neill had rejected the suggestion that Haissem Hassan had been omitted from the squad which faced Kilmarnock because he needed a kick up the backside. Yet, curiously, there was no sign of the Egyptian again here.

With Benjamin Nygren and Mika Baur injured, O’Neill hoped that a combination of McGregor, McCowan and Oxlade-Chamberlain would have enough.

Sources indicate that kasper Hogh’s chances of ending a run of 16 games without a goal weren’t helped by him starting on the bench. He didn’t leave it.

With just one win in nine coming into this, Craig McLeish’s side were short on points yet they were not short on confidence.

Although they played some stuff which was very easy on the eye, an inability to keep the ball out of the net cost them dear again.

It has been revealed that mcCowan had an early shot blocked before Colby Donovan had a weak effort saved. McCowan also hesitated to take a first-time strike with Louis Jackson doing enough to protect Jacob Chapman’s goal.

Industry observers note that celtic actually had the ball in the net twice before they made it count. Duran planted a header and a shot in the visitors’ net only to discover that the offside flag had been raised.

Recent findings suggest that jota sparked a sweeping move which saw Yang Hyun-jun tee up McCowan. Paul Nsio became the latest Saints player to frustrate the Celtic midfielder with a block.

Saints were aggrieved that Yang won a free-kick by going to ground too easily just before the opener. They may have had a point. That didn’t excuse the defending which followed.

Cameron Carter-Vickers rolled the ball in Yang’s direction. The winger burst away from Declan John and assessed his options.

It has been revealed that his cut-back for the unmarked Oxlade-Chamberlain was inch-perfect. The former England midfielder swept home his first goal since netting against the same opponent in April.

Saints might well have levelled immediately. Ismeal Kabia wriggled away from Donovan and picked out Eseosa Sule. Liam Scales did well to prevent the forward netting from seven yards.

Celtic then cut through Saints with embarrassing ease. A straight pass sent Yang clear on goal. He should have gone for glory, but instead tried to square the ball to allow Duran a tap-in. Alex Gogic had other ideas and knocked the ball away for a corner.

Celtic midfielder Luke McCowan and St Mirren's Paul Nsio battle for the ball.

McLeish’s hopes of making it to the break still in the contest unravelled in the final five minutes of the first period.

Industry observers note that kieran Tierney’s decision to swap flanks paid dividends with a brilliant in-swinging cross. Duran ghosted onto it and cushioned the ball beyond Chapman with his left foot to claim his 14th goal of his debut season.

Jota might well have made it three-nil seconds later and he fired Oxlade-Chamberlain’s lay-off straight at the keeper.

There was no hope for Chapman as Celtic all but wrapped up the win three minutes before the interval.

Tierney was again the provider, his energy taking him to the line and allowing him to cross. McCowan calmly stroked home his second goal of the season.

Saints kept going seeking a goal which might have made it interesting. Kabia’s strike forced Sam Johnstone into a smart stop down to his right.

Yang ought to have killed the contest but blazed over while leaning back. Skipper McGregor demonstrated him how to do it as he buried a right foot shot low in the bottom left-hand corner from the edge of the box after a defender had taken the ball off Duran’s toe.

Saints did get on the board thanks to Phillips’ penalty conversion, the award coming after Johnstone clattered Calvin Ramsay as he punched clear.

According to recent reports, O’Neill was still able to send on Shim Mheaka and James Forrest with Austin Trusty returning to warm applause. Joel van den Berg had already been introduced for his debut along with Callum Osmand. The Dutch teenager demonstrated up well.

Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "After the referee lifted my hand to show I'm now a two-time world champion, it was a very overwhelming feeling," Mariam Bsharat mentioned.
  • According to recent reports, themes of relief, joy and sacrifice are commonplace in the reflections of athletes after a big win.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"After the referee lifted my hand to show I'm now a two-time world champion, it was a very overwhelming feeling," Mariam Bsharat mentioned. "Making history once is something, but making it twice is really something else. I felt very happy and I felt a massive relief. Only I know how many sacrifices I made and how many hardships I needed to overcome.".

According to recent reports, themes of relief, joy and sacrifice are commonplace in the reflections of athletes after a big win. In Mariam Bsharat's case, it's about more than just dedication to training and taking care of the body. The 17-year-old won her second under-21 World Karate Championship gold medal competing for the Palestine national team in Poland in October.

"It was everyday life, seeing people get killed around me and houses getting bombed," she told DW of her upbringing in the occupied West Bank.

In a recent development, "I faced challenges in transportation," Bsharat said. "I wasn't able to go from one city to another to be able to train with other people, so that I can actually prepare for competitions. I needed to travel to other countries like Jordan or Egypt ... which was very hard for me. And, financially, the support wasn't really the support an elite athlete needed.".

In a recent development, growing up in Nablus, Bsharat had a narrow path to the top. But initially, it was her own reluctance that threatened to stop a champion career before it started.

"When I was a little kid, I did not really love it," mentioned Bsharat, who competes in the division for fighters who weigh under 66 kilograms (145 pounds).

According to recent reports, "I started it because my family was in that sport," Bsharat said. "My father had a dojo, and my mother also did that sport. My siblings and my aunts and my uncles — it's a family thing. I started it because they were all doing it. In time, I started getting into it.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that family has been a constant source of comfort and inspiration for Bsharat. Her father and uncle have acted as manager and coach respectively. While her mother and siblings moved with Mariam to Hamburg, Germany, last year, her father remained in order to take care of his business, the dojo, though he visits and tries to be with his daughter in competitions. Integration has been made easier by her mastery of the language, taught to her by her German mother.

Bsharat has mixed feelings about leaving her homeland.

According to recent reports, "I'm thankful to be here because being in Germany opened lot of doors for me, and I think I have a brighter future here," Bsharat said. "But also being in Palestine was just my everyday life, and I loved it there. My family was around me, my friends were around me, and I just felt comfortable, which was a big change coming here to Germany. I think every change comes with hardships.".

Sources indicate that as well as the obvious difficulties of living in an area occupied by Israel, there are particular challenges for sportspeople living in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, with access to facilities, travel and constant security fears among them. As such, very few people from the Palestinian territories become successful on the international sporting stage. That, Bsharat mentioned, gives her responsibilities that are unusual and heavy for a person of any age, let alone a 17-year-old.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that "Being an elite athlete in Palestine is something very special because not everybody in Palestine has that opportunity. There aren't really a lot of athletes that are elite and who win international medals,” Bsharat remarked.

"So all that pressure from all the country and all the people, the family, the coaches are on me because I'm representing them, raising their flag,” she stated. "I sometimes even forget to fight for myself and actually think about myself.".

Recent findings suggest that that has not yet proved a barrier to Bsharat, who is is ranked first in the world in her category by the World Karate Federation (WKF). With Palestine recognized by the International Olympic Committee, Bsharat would likely have been a contender to raise that flag in Los Angeles at the 2028 Olympics. But the sport was dropped from the Games in 2024.

"The global karate community remains steadfast in our belief that the natural place for karate is within the Olympic Games, and we sincerely hope that the incongruence we suffered in Paris 2024 and LA 2028 will be corrected for Brisbane 2032, if not sooner," the WKF wrote in response to the decision in 2024. The sport was also taken off the slate for the recent Youth Games in Senegal.

Should karate return in Brisbane, Bsharat would likely be approaching her prime. In the meantime, she is looking forward to starting her journey as a senior when she turns 18. But she won't be hanging around.

"My goal is it to be a world champion at seniors, which is the hardest and the best thing you can achieve in karate," she stated.

"But winning an Olympic medal, being called Olympic champion or just representing my country with that flag [is a thought that] is just full of happiness and pride.".

The interview was conducted by Janek Speight.

Tottenham Hotspur recorded three successive home Premier League wins for the first time in two years as they swept Ipswich Town aside on Saturday afternoon.

Tottenham were looking to bounce back from a disappointing 1-0 defeat to Leeds United at Elland Road before the international break, and Roberto De Zerbi made the substantial call to hand 18-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett his first competitive start for the club on the left wing.

Spurs fans have long been calling to see the teenager handed a start after what they had seen from the youngster in pre-season and in glimpses off the substitutes' bench this term, and his Italian manager decided to blood him in the absence of the injured Mathys Tel.

It was still a significant decision given Dejan Kulusevski, Omar Marmoush and Savio were named on the substitutes' bench, but he repaid his manager's faith with a stunning display that will surely see him retain his spot against Sunderland next Sunday.

Williams-Barnett took just 15 minutes to open his account for the club as he finished from close range following a fine cross from the right by Pedro Porro, before assisting Dominic Solanke's goal in the second half following a low ball in from the left flank.

The 18-year-old was a huge threat throughout his 64 minutes on the pitch, and mucked in from a defensive point of view as well to help the team keep a clean sheet.

Williams-Barnett for Tottenham vs Ipswich.

Williams-Barnett will take all the plaudits, and rightly so, but his teammate Porro was also influential in the victory against the Tractor Boys.

In a summer when Tottenham paid £100m to sign a player, and brought in nine more, arguably their best bit of summer business was tying Porro down to a new long-term contract at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Fresh on the back of winning the World Cup with Spain, there would have been concerns that the 27-year-old would attract interest from some of Europe's biggest clubs, especially after interest from Barcelona and Real Madrid previously.

However, Porro had already committed his future to Spurs by penning a five-year deal in June, extending his stay in North London even though the club only escaped relegation to the Championship on the final day of last season.

There have been a few ups and downs in terms of his performances this term, including a poor outing against Leeds last time out, but the Spaniard was back to his best and on top form against Ipswich.

As we mentioned previously, it was his cross that gave Williams-Barnett his first goal in a Tottenham shirt, and his display led to him actually being given a higher rating than the teenager on Fotmob (8.3 compared to 8.1).

He did everything he could to help Spurs in the final third, while he also completed his defensive duties to help the hosts keep a clean sheet.

Tottenham have made a significant improvement after a tough start to the season under De Zerbi's leadership, and there is no doubt that they look a much better team when Porro is on his game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sixteen-year-old Summer McIntosh broke the world record for the 400m individual medley at the Canadian swimming trials on Saturday – just days after breaking the world record for the 400m freestyle.

McIntosh finished the 400m individual medley in a time of 4:25.87, breaking the mark set at the 2016 Rio Olympics by Hungarian swimmer Katinka Hosszú with a time of 4:26.36.

The result continues the teenager’s brilliant week after she broke the 400m freestyle world record last Tuesday – breaking defending Olympic champion Ariarne Titmus’ previous record of 3:56.40, which was set last May, in a time of 3:56.08.

Speaking after her latest triumph, McIntosh shared her emotions.

“That’s the first time I really vividly heard the crowd during my race,” McIntosh said, per Reuters.

In a recent development, “It’s amazing to have all my family and friends in the stands, cheering me on. It really helped me in the last 100 meters.”.

The Canadian teen made her Olympic debut aged 14 at Tokyo 2020, where she finished fourth in the 200-meter freestyle.

She bagged gold in the 200m butterfly and 400m medley at the world championships in 2022, as well as two golds at the Commonwealth Games in the 200m and 400m medleys.

She now trains in Florida under coach Brent Arckey with the Sarasota Sharks team.

Tijjani Noslin found the net twice before Davide Frattesi put the cherry on top with a delightful lob in the final minutes of the match.

“I am proud of the mentality and the hunger shown by the team today,” Gattuso told DAZN Italia.

There is always some concern for coaches after the break for international duty, but Gattuso assures he had no such qualms about his Lazio players.

“I saw the way they were training, so I was not worried. There is a great spirit and application, we’ve got to keep going like this. It is all down to the players, they are putting in the right mentality, hunger and sense of belonging. They are doing something incredible.”.

Nicolò Rovella also came off the bench late on and is still trying to work his way back to full fitness after numerous complications.

“Rovella can give us more vertical passes, as when he gets the ball, he immediately looks up and forward,” explained the coach.

Sources indicate that “I think we also need to talk about Fisayo Dele-Bashiru. He deserves more. We’ve got to give Rovella playing time so that he can regain fitness, then he can give us an important hand.”.

Considering how well Lazio are doing under Gattuso so far this season, is there anything he still hasn’t seen and wants them to improve?

In a recent development, “I don’t mind losing the ball with misplaced passes that much, because when you play at a high tempo, that can happen. I am more interested in the mentality of the side and how they are hanging in there under pressure.

Industry observers note that “I am satisfied, you always want something more, but at this tempo there are going to be some misplaced passes. We can improve our reading of the game, as for example today when we struggled to get through the middle, we needed to spread the game out wide.”.

Former Everton midfielder Leon Osman has praised David Moyes’ enduring legacy in the blue half of Merseyside, insisting the Scotsman’s Glaswegian grit made him the ideal fit the club.

Moyes transformed Everton’s fortunes during an 11-year spell on Merseyside between 2002 and 2013, consistently guiding the Toffees into the top half of the Premier League despite operating on a fraction of the transfer budgets enjoyed by their top-flight rivals.

While Moyes never lifted a major trophy during his tenure - falling just short in the 2009 FA Cup final against Chelsea - Osman believes his former boss’s ability to punch above his weight cements his status as one of the club’s most vital modern figures.

"For the majority of David Moyes' time in charge of Everton, he's probably overachieved in terms of what he's had to spend in the transfer market, so while he might not have had the success Harry Catterick did in terms of silverware, he's been so notable for the club," Osman told Betway.

In a recent development, "He's a great fit for Everton, and I think it's that Glaswegian way that adapts particularly well to Liverpool because there's a real understanding of what the people of the city are like and what they want to see from their football team. Everton is the people's club first and foremost, and the fans want to see the team work hard and show that desire to be successful and that's something David Moyes has always instilled in his teams.".

It has been revealed that osman was a central pillar of that Moyes era, making over 400 appearances for his boyhood club after breaking into the senior squad under the manager’s guidance. However, the former England international admitted he initially faced an uphill battle to prove he possessed the physicality required for top-flight football before becoming one of Moyes' most trusted lieutenants.

According to recent reports, "He's the man who gave me my shot in the Premier League, so I'll always be thankful to him for that," Osman added. "It did take me a while, though, to convince him I was able and I was ready to play at that level, but once he gave me that chance I think he realised that we had very similar outlooks in terms of style of play and how the game should be played and we had a really great relationship throughout my career.".

  • Daniel Farke's side came out of the international break with a superb performance as they hit back immediately from going a goal down to dominate the rest of the proceedings on the way to a 4-1 victory.
  • It was the visitors' first win at Stamford Bridge this century and saw United overtake their hosts in the Premier League table as they climbed to sixth, thanks to an Okafor brace, a penalty from Dominic Calvert-Lewin, and Brenden Aaronson's late fourth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Attacking standouts such as Noah Okafor will take the headlines after Leeds United dismantled Chelsea at Stamford Bridge but the man who unlocked that performance deserves just as many accolades.

Daniel Farke's side came out of the international break with a superb performance as they hit back immediately from going a goal down to dominate the rest of the proceedings on the way to a 4-1 victory.

It was the visitors' first win at Stamford Bridge this century and saw United overtake their hosts in the Premier League table as they climbed to sixth, thanks to an Okafor brace, a penalty from Dominic Calvert-Lewin, and Brenden Aaronson's late fourth.

Emmanuel Emegha had opened the scoring in the 25th minute with his first goal for Chelsea, but Okafor cancelled it out moments later as he slid the equaliser into the far corner with the Blues' defence panicking as he entered the box.

Michael Oliver awarded Leeds a penalty early in the second half when a shot was blocked by Morgan Rogers' arm, with insufficient evidence available to VAR to say whether it had hit him above the T-shirt line and whether they could overturn it, with Calvert-Lewin stepping up to send Emi Martinez the wrong way.

Okafor doubled the lead just five minutes later to effectively end the contest, slamming into the top corner from a deflected ball across the area, and substitute Aaronson rounded things off in stoppage time as he surged clear and cut inside before slipping the ball between Martinez's legs.

But as impressive as the Whites were in attack, the game was won in midfield, where Chelsea lost Moises Caicedo to injury mid-way through the first half and subsequently failed to regain any sort of control.

It is difficult to pick just one from Leeds' central midfield pairing of ex-Blue Ethan Ampadu and Ao Tanaka, but the Japanese international was outstanding on the day.

The Yorkshire Evening Post rated him 9/10 following the final whistle, and it wasn't hard to see why after his excellent work in and out of possession, particularly as his side took charge after the break.

Tanaka was ably supported by Ampadu as they took full advantage of Chelsea losing one of their £100 million men, leaving replacement Jordan Henderson, and Romeo Lavia, over-matched in the middle.

As is so often the case on Leeds' best days under Farke, including on previous occasions against the same opposition, Tanaka was the heartbeat of the side as he moved the ball around efficiently and didn't give his opposite numbers time to think.

Stats compiled by FotMob indicate the 28-year-old was highly effective with his 59 touches across 86 minutes on the pitch, as he bounced back from a series of early fouls conceded to shine as the game went on.

With the ball at his feet, Tanaka kept Leeds moving efficiently, completing 43 of his 49 passes, and wasn't dispossessed once on the day, while his defensive contributions also made a real difference.

The Leeds man made a pair of successful tackles, two interceptions, and seven recoveries of possession, and wasn't dribbled past once as part of an excellent display all round.

Chelsea simply couldn't put together enough passes to threaten getting back into the game as Tanaka and his teammates didn't give them the time or space to regroup, while operating with far more zip when going the other way.

Okafor's finishes will deservedly take much of the focus, but the attacking platform provided by the midfield was vital, just as it was in ensuring James Trafford was relatively untested at the back.

A first Stamford Bridge win since 1999 appeared to be on the cards earlier this season when Farke took his side to West London in the Carabao Cup, only for it to be snatched away during a chaotic second half in September.

Leeds led 2-0 at the break before a Cole Palmer penalty sparked a turnaround which resulted in a 6-3 Chelsea victory and extended the run without a victory at this ground by one more game.

It was very much the reverse on Saturday afternoon as the hosts this time went ahead but collapsed themselves following the interval to see Farke and his players depart with a vital three points.

And on current evidence it is unlikely to be another 27 years until Leeds get another win away at one of their old rivals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the millions who cast their ballots in the US midterm elections, one issue ranked above all others: the economy.

So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?

Markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively. Global stocks rallied as investors appeared to take heart from the Democrats' victory.

With Democrats now holding comfortable majorities in both houses of Congress and Trump still in the White House, it could lead to gridlock in Washington. Trump has already stated he would become "Mr Veto," meaning he would block any legislation the Democrats advance.

"The magnitude of the gains for the Democrats in the midterms does not change too much for the near-term policy outlook, given the party still lacks a filibuster-proof majority in the Senate and President Trump has veto power to block legislation," Stephen Brown, chief North America economist with Capital Economics, said in a note.

It has been revealed that "I think we are looking at two years of complete 100% gridlock," Jacob Funk Kirkegaard, nonresident senior fellow with the Peterson Institute for International Economics, told DW after the results came in. "Nothing will get done of any kind.".

Some investors appear worried that the Democrats could force through AI regulation, especially if they also win the White House in 2028. Rising opposition among large majorities of the US population to data centers — the key infrastructure behind AI — helped secure victories for many Democratic candidates.

It has been revealed that kirkegaard, who is also a senior fellow at Bruegel, a European economics think tank, mentioned the vote showed the extent of that opposition. Even if the Democrats can't force regulation, he thinks local opposition will make it harder for data centers to be built, which could hit the valuation of significant tech firms that have benefitted from the AI boom.

In a recent development, "This election demonstrates that the political underpinning of the rapid, aggressive AI growth story is shaky," he said. "It doesn't mean it's going to stop or be made illegal, but the dynamic of the growth story has shifted.".

If the Democrats were to win the presidency in 2028, Brown remarked, they would be perfectly placed to make major policy changes. "That includes the potential for tax hikes on corporations and high-income individuals as well as regulation that could delay the AI rollout," he said.

According to polling conducted in early October by the Pew Research Center, 56% of Americans say Trump's tariff policies will have mostly negative impacts on the country, with only 20% saying mostly positive.

That sentiment clearly drove many Democrats to victory in the midterms — particularly in states where tariffs have had a particularly negative impact. That includes those with sectors reliant on exports, such as Texas, Michigan, Iowa and Illinois, where counter-tariffs have hit and those that have high trade volumes with Canada.

Yet, barring an unprecedented climbdown from Trump — who has been ideologically wedded to tariffs since he first became a public figure almost 50 years ago — it's not clear how the Democrats could force substantial change to the president's signature economic policy.

Industry observers note that "Trump will not be moderated," Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Hinrich Foundation in Singapore, told DW earlier this year. "Expect him to continue his trade disruption and tariff policies for as long as he remains in the Oval Office.".

Though the US Constitution gives Congress the power to collect and organize tariffs, various laws passed over the years have given presidents power to implement tariffs when they cite certain conditions, such as national security or economic emergencies.

Trump has already used such avenues for his tariffs and can continue to do so, despite some legal rebukes. However, while Congress can't necessarily force an end to Trump's existing tariffs, it can now take further legal action against them to prevent greater escalation.

Though Trump and the Democrats are clearly not going to make common cause, Kirkegaard stated, the scale of the Republicans' defeat might force Trump to be less erratic in his policymaking, from escalating his trade war with Canada to his Iran policy.

Trump said in the aftermath of Tuesday's defeats that he would "work with" the Democrats and told the Financial Times in the run-up to the vote that he was unlikely to escalate the war in Iran.

Were a deal to be struck with Iran, soaring energy prices — a pivotal election issue — could finally fall, helping voters with their cost-of-living concerns.

"You've got to get a deal with Iran, and you've got to bring down gas prices," Kirkegaard mentioned. "From a political point of view, that's the most key thing now.".

George Saravelos, an analyst with Deutsche Bank FX Research, thinks the markets are beginning to become more optimistic in that area. "With oil flows through the Middle East having materially recovered, the market is pricing a large imminent risk premium of re-escalation and energy supply disruption," he mentioned in a note.

Despite the scale of the Democrats' victory, the fact that Trump remains in the Oval Office will complicate all efforts to force a change to signature economic policies and challenges.

Recent findings suggest that yet Congress can now exert considerable pressure. Another glitch vital to voters was corruption and the belief that the Trump administration has engaged in corruption and personal enrichment while in office.

That raises the prospect of the new Democratic-controlled Congress launching legal investigations and potentially pursuing another impeachment of Trump, which could force the president to negotiate on some economic issues to secure his political survival.

"Can you find 10 or 12 Republican senators who, in the face of overwhelming corruption, would be willing to vote for articles of impeachment? I wouldn't rule it out," Kirkegaard noted. "And that's a scenario in which Trump might suddenly be much more accommodating to, for instance, abandoning most of his tariffs.".

Despite voters' clear rejection of Trump's economic policies, the Democratic Party's newly minted senators, congressmen and congresswomen face an uphill battle in trying to reverse them.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Aston Villa vs Manchester City.

Premier League leaders City will attempt to maintain their flawless start to the season when they visit Villa Park for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

The match marks the first meeting between the sides since the final weekend of last season, when Villa secured a 2-1 victory at the Etihad in Pep Guardiola’s final game in charge at City.

According to recent reports, enzo Maresca became the first manager in City’s Premier League history to win his opening seven fixtures, lifting his side three points clear of title holders Arsenal. Only Chelsea in 2005-06 and Liverpool in 2019-20 have managed a longer winning start to a top-flight campaign. Following a 3-2 victory against Ipswich Town last weekend, City rebounded from a European setback against Paris Saint-Germain by delivering a commanding 5-1 Champions League win over AEK Athens on Wednesday.

However, Unai Emery’s side will present a formidable challenge. Aston Villa enter the contest on a seven-match unbeaten streak across all competitions, headlined by a perfect record in the Champions League following midweek success against Viking FK.

Villa’s domestic form has also improved, taking seven points from their last three league outings, including a 1-0 away victory at Newcastle United in Emery’s 100th Premier League match as manager. Sitting 12th in the table, Villa remain on the hunt for their first home league win of the season, though their impressive European performances at Villa Park provide significant momentum.

Emery’s men completed a league double over City last term, including a 1-0 win on home turf. Should Villa claim victory again on Saturday, it would mark the first time in the Premier League era that they have recorded three consecutive victories over the Manchester club.

Of course, City’s campaign remains overshadowed by the recent guilty verdict from the Premier League over financial regulations.

“I love Adrien, he’s one of my favourite players. I think he’s fantastic, and I have a tremendous amount of respect for him and his family. We’re in discussions and I hope we’ll get a good result. If it were up to me, he’d be a franchise player for this team.”.

Fourth-placed Milan face sixth-placed Frosinone on Sunday at 18:00 CET [17:00 GMT].

Arsenal had to settle for a 2-2 draw away to Newcastle United in a chaotic game that has raised question marks about two of Mikel Arteta's players.

Just when it looked likely the Gunners were running away with the Premier League title, the Magpies came along. Matthias Jaissle came into the game under pressure amid a disappointing start to his reign, and his side were expected to suffer a fifth league defeat.

Sources indicate that when Eberechi Eze's 33rd-minute opener went in, it looked set to be a long night for Jaissle and his team. They were outplayed throughout the first half, but came out a different side after the break, taking the game to the defending champions.

Harvey Barnes equalised in the 49th minute to lift the mood at St James' Park before a pinball-like scenario in the visitors' box led to pandemonium in the 62nd minute. Malick Thiaw pounced to poke the ball into the back of the net and give his side a shock lead.

Sources indicate that that lead lasted until the 78th minute when Noni Madueke did superbly well to find the bottom corner. Mikel Arteta couldn't hide his delight on the touchline, though he wouldn't have been pleased with dropping two points.

In a recent development, one of the major talking points heading into tonight's game centred on Bruno Guimaraes' return to Tyneside. The manner of his departure in the summer left a sour taste in Newcastle fans' mouths, and they let him know it every time he touched the ball.

Recent findings suggest that guimaraes didn't have anywhere near the impact he'd have hoped for, and Arteta's midfield overall wasn't quite up to the high standards we've come to expect from them. Once the Gunners took the lead, they should have kicked on and secured all three points, but instead they allowed the hosts back into the game.

A frustrating night for Arteta was made even worse when David Raya suffered an injury and had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga in the second half. Coming out of November's international break, he probably viewed this fixture favourably, yet a strange affair has thrown up a fair few concerns.

Sources indicate that arsenal fans haven't had much to complain about so far this season, certainly not the performances of Martin Odegaard. The Norwegian endured a frustrating previous campaign due to injury issues, unable to play a star role in his side's title win.

Odegaard has been back to his best this term, but his display at St James' Park didn't live up to expectations. Likewise, Guimaraes' subdued return as an opponent led to frustration among his current club's fanbase.

Supporters have largely blamed the pair for the dropped points, with one writing: "ODEGAARD AND BRUNO GUIMARAES OFF ASAP! They are off the pace in this game. Killing us.".

Another fan added: "Odegaard and Guimaraes are too weak in midfield.".

One supporter bemoaned a perceived lack of effort: "Odegaard and Bruno Guimaraes simply don't deserve to play with some of these very special players we have. How about they bloody contribute?".

Another expressed doubts over the summer fee: "Still yet to be convinced that spending £75m on Guimaraes was wise.".

One fan added: "Bruno Guimaraes and Martin Odegaard midfield would never work. Both of them seem to be running away from any form of contact. It’s the main reason we ain’t winning this game.".

Another took issue with Arteta's skipper and his leadership: "Odegaard is no captain quality.".

Arteta has plenty of midfield options in his squad, including Myles Lewis-Skelly, who came on for Guimaraes, as well as Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. He'll be hoping for an improvement from his team when they host Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday.

Published: 12:38 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:28 EST, 21 November 2026.

Recent findings suggest that this is all becoming rather inevitable at Bournemouth. Will they ever stop winning? Will Evanilson ever stop scoring?

The numbers alone are astonishing. Nine wins on the bounce for the first time in their history, their victory here against Nottingham Forest making it six on the spin at home at an aggregate score of 15 to nil. Five wins in a row in the Premier League for the first time, too, a result that moved them into the top four.

In a recent development, this is Bournemouth, remember. Only this is Bournemouth now.

In a recent development, make no mistake: this is no hot streak. This is not a team under Marco Rose carried to win after win after win on a wave of momentum and vibes. This is relentless, breathtaking stuff. This is a team that, week after week, outplays every team that stands in front of them. It doesn’t matter if it’s Forest, or Manchester United, or AC Milan. Bournemouth turn up and they blow their opponents away.

They move it quicker and sharper, they win it back faster and higher. They give teams no time to think or breathe, so it’s little wonder they have no answer.

‘We never really struggled, remarked Rose. 'We suffered a little bit at the end, but we defended quite well together, and that's why it's a deserved win.

Bournemouth racked up their sixth successive league victory and ninth in all competitions.

Recent findings suggest that 'If we use the right approach every game – and this is really, really demanding – we win games. Next game, we have to prove it again. If we do it, then we can keep the level up. But as I said, this is a tough job.

Recent findings suggest that ‘The collective is strong, but even this we have to maintain. Because if you win games…I mean, some of our players right now are in a lot of noise and rumours.

'If we are able to keep these kinds of things away from the locker room, and if everyone comes into training every day, works hard and gives everything for the club and the team, then we are really, really good.'.

The only real surprise was that Evanilson, Bournemouth’s talismanic Brazilian, didn’t leave with more than just his one, now customary, goal.

That itself was another fine finish after Tyler Adams won the ball high up the pitch – obviously – dinked it across to James Hill, back after his first England call-up, who flicked a header into Evanilson’s path. He thumped it past Matz Sels to do the rest.

Industry observers note that rose, who called him a ‘real No9’ the other week, had been urging him to get into the box more to finish off chances. He did that, all right. Twice earlier in the game, he raced on to through balls only to be denied by Sels and a last-ditch tackle from Jair Cunha.

It has been revealed that his opening strike, his eighth goal in his last nine games, means he is the first Premier League player to reach double figures for goal contributions with six goals alongside his four other assists. He leads the press, he creates chances, he scores goals. He does the lot.

Sources indicate that that’s now six league games in a row he’s found the net, halfway to breaking Jamie Vardy’s record of 11 in a row. You wouldn’t put it past him.

Bournemouth’s talismanic Brazilian Evanilson scored for the sixth successive league match.

Recent findings suggest that forest came into this, after all, off the back of a huge, much-needed victory against Manchester City. After just one win in Oliver Glasner’s opening nine league games, that was the performance those around Forest felt that could spark the season into life.

It was also meant to be the one where Liam Delap’s Forest career burst into life with two thunderous goals in a bullying, battering-ram showing.

Alas, they both ran into a proper team this week.

Forest tried to go direct to Delap, partly to try to bypass the intense Bournemouth press, but nothing stuck. Delap lost possession with 23 of his 39 touches. He committed more fouls than he had shots and found his way into the referee’s book for clumsily bundling over Adam Smith.

The visitors huffed and puffed in the second half but never really looked like scoring. The closest they got was a couple of speculative long-range efforts from Morgan Gibbs-White and James McAtee before a late goalmouth scramble nearly provided an opening through chaos more than creativity.

It was only the busy hands of Sels that kept the scoring respectable.

In a recent development, ’The defeat was deserved,’ noted Glasner. ‘City and today were completely different. It's like a different sport. This is football, but it's different.

Industry observers note that 'When teams play like City, when it's more of a tactical game, we are doing well. When it's more of a physical, intense game, we're struggling. Today our weaknesses came to the surface.’.

When asked if he had the players to play this way, Glasner responded: 'Right now, I have to say no. If not, we will add players. If we believe we need somebody to add this physicality, these quick solutions, we will do it.'.

Did they expect much else, though? Forest never beat Bournemouth. That’s 13 meetings in a row now they have failed to win.

‘Nottingham Forest, it’s happened again,’ sang the home fans in the final few minutes.

Liam Delap and Nottingham Forest crashed into a proper team as they came back down to earth after their win over Man City before the international break.

Marcus Tavernier's performances could get a chance with England if he maintains his form.

Bournemouth have already had a couple of deserved England call-ups this season in Hill and midfielder Alex Scott. How long until Marcus Tavernier gets his chance?

No English player has scored more Premier League goals this season than the Bournemouth winger, level with Morgan Rogers and Dominic Calvert-Lewin, and once again he was at the heart of everything good the Cherries do.

Industry observers note that his superb cross behind the Forest defence found Justin Kluivert for Bournemouth’s second of the afternoon. He danced through the Forest defence to set up Rayan for a late chance.

'It was my 11th Premier League game today, and I couldn't see better offensive midfielders so far this season,’ noted Rose.

In a recent development, ‘If you see how he works and how he plays, the quality he has, he scores goals. He's 27, he's at the best age.

‘If he plays well, if he stays healthy, I think, like with Hilly, these things come. They're just around the corner.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that today, as of 10:16 GMT, NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft has journeyed one light-day, or 25.9 billion kilometres, from Earth — farther than any human-made object has gone before. At this distance, signals from Earth’s surface travelling at light speed will take a full 24 hours to reach the craft. The trailblazing probe is expected to lose communications with Earth in 2029, when its plutonium power finally dies. But that time might not signal the end of Voyager 1’s contributions — the craft carries a golden record engraved with sights and sounds from Earth, an interspecies message for any aliens who might encounter it as it continues its journey.

Sources indicate that A device that stimulates the brain with flickering light and rhythmic clicking sounds has failed to slow memory loss in people with Alzheimer’s disease. The Spectris AD headset is designed to induce brain activity called gamma waves, which have been linked to increased attention and memory. The results of a long-anticipated clinical trial showed that participants who used the device did not show robust improvements in their cognitive function after a year of treatment compared with those assigned to a sham treatment. The results were reported at the Clinical Trials on Alzheimer's Disease meeting on 16 November.

Recent findings suggest that the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) has announced that the United States has lost its measles elimination status amid an outbreak that’s caused more than 5,700 infections and 10 deaths this year. The US had eliminated measles in 2000 after an intensive vaccination campaign. But declining vaccination rates in the past few years have left pockets of the population vulnerable to infection. “We’ve taken an enormous step back in public health,” notes virologist Paul Offit. Measles has also been re-established in Mexico and Bolivia, PAHO announced.

Source: International Vaccine Access Center, Johns Hopkins University.

Consumer tests that promise to reveal the full range of microbes living in your gut are taking off — but their results can vary widely. “This is an industry that’s running wild,” indicates genomicist Jacques Ravel, who co-authored a study that tested several providers. With regard to testing methods, he says, “there’s no standard”. But it’s hard to set those standards, writes journalist Amber Dance, who sent off her own stool to investigate the field. Part of the problem is that “there is no known ‘ground truth’ for a natural microbial sample”, she says.

In a recent development, the proportion of reviewers at Nature who are early-career researchers. Increasing it would benefit all researchers and science as a whole, argues a Nature editorial. (Nature | 6 min read).

In a recent development, amid the tedium of investigating potentially fraudulent papers, “there is some light relief, thanks to some hilarious phrases used by authors seeking to avoid detection by plagiarism checkers”, writes research-integrity sleuth Dorothy Bishop. Bishop and Nature’s careers team have compiled a quiz to test your ability to match ‘tortured phrases’ — those that replace common words with synonyms in an attempt to skirt past plagiarism-detection software — with their original text.

From the Bering Strait to Doggerland, much of human history occurred in places that are now underwater, covered by the sea-level rise that occurs after ice ages. Geographer Jerome Dobson has dubbed this drowned land ‘Aquaterra’. It’s the site of many discoveries — such as Blinkerwall in the Baltic Sea, one of Europe’s oldest and largest Stone Age structures — and possibly many more to come. It also offers an interesting thought experiment: if we continue to drive global warming, what might future archaeologists make of our inundated world?

The Atlantic | 29 min read, intermittent paywall.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cristiano Ronaldo took to social media on Thursday to announce that he had played his last game for Portugal.

"To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No. 7 shirt of our national team," the 41-year-old Ronaldo mentioned in a video on his Instagram account.

"I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world," Ronaldo said.

The former Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus forward represented his country 234 times, scoring 146 goals — making him the men's record-holder for ⁠international ​appearances and for international goals.

He captained Portugal ​to their first major trophy at ​Euro 2016 and led them to the 2019 and 2025 Nations League titles.

"It was not an easy decision, there are decisions that are not ​only with the head. They are also made with the heart," Ronaldo continued in the Instagram post.

"If I ever made you happy, ​if one of my goals ever made you hug someone, forget a worry or feel ⁠proud ​of our country, then it ​was all worth it.".

He also thanked his family, the Portuguese people ​and the teammates, coaches and staff he worked with over his national ​team career.

The Portuguese Football Association (FPF) released a statement expressing its gratitude and respect for the player also known as "CR7.".

"Cristiano Ronaldo has raised Portugal's profile and inspired generations of young people who dream of following in his footsteps; for many of us, he is the greatest player of all time!" it read.

The FPF intends to organize a tribute "in which the fans and the country can one more time applaud and celebrate a player who has given us so much.".

While his long-rival Lionel Messi ended his Argentina career with a much anticipated farewell match last month, Ronaldo's final appearance may go down as Portugal's 1-0 win over Wales on September 24, depending on the nature of the tribute. Portugal coach Jorge Jesus left him on the bench for the following match and remarked he wouldn't start the next one.

Ronaldo responded by walking out of the Portugal training camp. He was subsequently suspended and fined by the FPF, but he had been expected to return to Portugal for the November international break.

Like Messi, Ronaldo intends to continue his club career with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia.

Upcoming Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino has suffered a blow ahead of his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday, as GIVEMESPORT understands that Marcus Rashford remains sidelined and won't be fit for the trip to Merseyside.

Pochettino failed to give an update on the fitness of his players in his first press conference on Friday, perhaps influenced by Drone-gate in the lead up to the major game at Anfield.

The Argentine will be determined to get off to a positive start as Man United manager, with the club lying in 19th position in the Premier League table after winning just one of their opening 10 top flight fixtures this term.

The Red Devils dropped a place in the table on Saturday after Sunderland picked up a point against Aston Villa at Villa Park to leapfrog them in the table, and they were fortunate that Crystal Palace were beaten by Coventry City in Thomas Frank's first game at the helm, otherwise they'd have been rock-bottom.

It won't be an easy task against Andoni Iraola's side, and Pochettino would have been hoping to welcome back some of his injured stars to help him on Merseyside.

There was anticipation that Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw and Rashford might all return to face Liverpool after various injury issues, and while there is no update on the former two yet, GMS understands that Rashford won't be available.

The fact that the 29-year-old remains sidelined with his ongoing hip glitch could also raise doubts over his availability for the trip to Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday in the Champions League.

United will also be without Benjamin Sesko and Carlos Baleba against Liverpool, with the duo also both on the sidelines because of injury, meaning Pochettino's options are limited in certain positions.

With reports suggesting that the Argentine has 'always loved' Rashford, being without him already will be a blow for the former Spurs boss.

With Sesko and Rashford both confirmed absentees for the trip to Anfield, United's frontline almost picks itself unless Pochettino is ready to make an unexpected pick.

Should the Red Devils line up in a 4-2-3-1 formation, it would be expected that Bruno Fernandes stays in the No.10 position, given we know the Argentine manager is a major fan of the Portugal international.

Fernandes has struggled to live up to the level he showed last season, but he continues to be their most influential player in the final third.

Pochettino could bring Joshua Zirkzee in from the fringes to play as a centre-forward, but starting Bryan Mbeumo there seems more likely given the Dutchman's lack of minutes this term.

If Mbeumo does start through the centre, then Amad Diallo and Matheus Cunha could get the nod on the flanks, although Shea Lacey is pushing for a starting spot after impressive cameos off the substitutes' bench against AS Roma and Aston Villa in recent weeks.

Elsewhere, Patrick Dorgu should start at left-back if Shaw isn't deemed fit enough, while Lisandro Martinez, Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans also appear likely to make the starting XI given the injury challenges in the squad.

Cesc Fabregas praised Jacobo Ramón’s attacking threat after the defender scored in Como’s 2-0 win over Cagliari, although he insisted the performance was far from perfect.

With quotes via TuttoMercatoWeb, Ramón headed Como in front from Yan Couto’s assist in the 24th minute, and Lucas Da Cunha added a second, also set up by Couto, early in the second half. The win takes Fabregas’ side up to fourth for now, and Como remain unbeaten at the Sinigaglia in Serie A this season.

In a recent development, “Perfect? No. We conceded four counter-attacks, three of them substantial chances where they could have scored,” Fabregas remarked. “They did something different going forward and found space in behind us, but from around the 35th minute things changed, and in the second half there was only one team on the pitch.

“I’m very happy for the lads. There was so much energy, and Lahdo came on very well. We had to finish with two right-backs because we don’t have the players. Today my only attacking option on the bench was Nico Paz.”.

Ramón has just been called up by Spain for the first time, and Fabregas believes his scoring has improved a lot.

“There are players who are stronger, but he’s a player I like. I won’t say too much about how I feel about him, because he might read it later,” Fabregas joked. “We worked a lot on his finishing. Last year he couldn’t score in front of goal, even easy chances. Now he scores them. It indicates you they’re kids, but they improve every year.

“He arrives in the box with more aggression than a striker, even when you don’t expect it, and he can play long and short. In the air, he’s first or second in Serie A for duels won. But if you want to reach the top, you have to handle Thuram and Esposito, so the lads understand they always have to do more to get to that level.

“In five or six years, I’d like to see all these lads playing at World Cups and winning the Champions League. They have the chance to grow here.”.

Da Cunha started despite his efforts with France this week, because Maxence Caqueret picked up a minor problem on Friday.

Sources indicate that “Honestly, I wanted to rest him today, but we can’t take risks now, we’re down to 11, 12, 13 players. He’s a gem for us. He always raises the level. I’d like every player in the world to have Da Cunha’s mentality.”.

He also warned there’s no room to ease off.

“There are seven games left before Christmas, and everyone has to play their part.”.

In a recent development, “Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, said of his £55m signing. “He’s come to a huge club and to position yourself in that manner, and to perform at the level he is, it is very difficult to do. We are really lucky to have him.”.

In a recent development, in Arsenal’s latest victory, their seventh from eight matches in the Premier League this season, Konsa offered all of his usual defensive security and calmness in possession. Even more excitingly, he also scored his first goal for the club, smashed in from close range after a corner had caused chaos in Everton’s penalty area. It was Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

Sources indicate that “I have been waiting to score my first goal for a while,” Konsa said. “I spoke to the set-piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well. We felt as players that it was coming, and today was the day.”.

In a recent development, some eyebrows were raised when Arsenal paid such a large fee to sign Konsa from Aston Villa. The Villa fans, though, were not among those who questioned the price or the player’s ability. They have known for years at Villa Park that Konsa is a player of the highest quality, and they will not be surprised by his exceptional start to his Arsenal career.

The same is true of the Arsenal players. Arteta asked the England internationals in his squad about Konsa before buying him, and the feedback was overwhelmingly positive. Konsa was already close friends with Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze before completing his transfer from Villa.

Industry observers note that konsa’s start to life at Arsenal is all the more impressive because he did not even have a pre-season. He effectively came straight from the World Cup into the club, and has been starting games since early September. According to recent reports, konsa, 29, has promptly built a strong relationship with Gabriel Magalhães, his defensive partner who scored Arsenal’s other goal here against Everton, from Ben White’s cross. For both centre-backs to find the net felt like a throwback to last year, when Arsenal were so dangerous from crosses, and underlined how Arteta’s team are capable of hurting their opponents in many different ways.

Sources indicate that the nature of the goals might give a misleading impression of Arsenal’s performance, though. This was not a gritty win. Arteta’s side produced some excellent passing moves and circulated the ball with menace throughout the game. They were also a little open at times, especially in the first half when Everton created a handful of decent chances.

It has been revealed that thierno Barry missed the best of those opportunities, with the score at 1-0. It was the closest the visitors came to hurting the champions, aside from some of James Tarkowski’s full-blooded tackles. “I felt we didn’t really get to a level that was good enough to get near them,” admitted David Moyes, the Everton manager.

The victory, combined with Manchester City’s defeat earlier in the day, put Arsenal level on points at the top of the table. Aside from the extraordinary thrashing at Brighton, Arteta’s side have looked just as solid, if not more so, than last season. That speaks volumes of the quality in the team, of course, but also indicates plenty about the way Konsa has adjusted to his newly introduced surroundings. Thanks to him, Saliba’s absence has not hurt at all.

“Great feeling, it always is. A clean sheet, a goal – my first goal for the club – so a fantastic day overall.

All over at the Emirates and the champions go level on points with Manchester City at the top of the table.

On what makes Arsenal difficult to play...

Industry observers note that “They’re reigning Premier League champions, a top side that has been knocking on the door to win the title for a few years before as well. They’re a team at a high level but this is what Premier League football is all about and it’s up to us to get a result.”.

So, yeah, we have to really be at it and be very aggressive from the beginning.”.

One of the clearest signs a football club is in a good place is when the debate switches from whether the team are winning to how they are winning.

Recent findings suggest that this is right now Arsenal and Mikel Arteta’s world. For years, Arsenal coaches and players were asked how and when they would start collecting major trophies again. With no concern about their capacity to challenge for top honours over the coming years, the style has become the main focus.

In a recent development, it’s a welcome “problem” – or some might argue a non-existent one – for Arteta while his side is so strong. Building a fortress is the expensive, time-consuming and difficult part. Once it’s constructed and established, how you decorate it is a matter of taste.

Whether neutrals will hold the current champions in the same regard as the great Arsène Wenger sides will be a trivial concern if Arteta does what no Arsenal manager has since 1935 – defend the league title – and then add a few more, which is a serious possibility based on the balance of power in England and the likely punishment heading Manchester City’s way.

For Everton, Jack Grealish misses today’s game due to sickness, while Jarrad Branthwaite is absent because of concussion protocols despite finishing last week’s match with Chelsea after a head collision with Emi Martinez.

Hello and welcome to coverage from the Emirates as Premier League champions Arsenal host Everton.

Mikel Arteta’s men produced a good performance in midweek to draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League while David Moyes’s squad have had the week off following their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea last weekend.

Arteta said: “We’re having three games in six days so we know what’s happening, especially when the games are so demanding and the necessity is to win. We know that, so we prepare the players for those scenarios and do the best we possibly can.

In a recent development, “I know David so well and how he sets the team, the quality they have in their organisation and individually. It’s no coincidence they didn’t lose before their last game. They have a really good team, which we know because in recent clashes, it’s always been a really difficult game for us.”.

Both teams enter this game having been beaten just once this season but eight points separate them with Arsenal in second and Everton in eighth.

Industry observers note that moyes stated: “It’s not an easy game and never has been over many years. We look forward to it; they had a game in midweek, and we have to try and capitalise on that. I thought we did really well last year against them; we played really well down at Arsenal, and I hope we can do the same.

Sources indicate that “When I look back at the team we had out, we were pretty threadbare at that time, but we did a good job, and I hope we can do it again. Obviously Arsenal have some many different tools in their bag and people they can use in different positions, so we’re fully aware of the team we’re up against and the level.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

LSU star Angel Reese defended the gesture she aimed at Iowa Hawkeyes’ Caitlin Clark near the end of the Tigers’ first NCAA women’s basketball national championship victory on Sunday, saying “I don’t take disrespect lightly.”.

Reese could be seen approaching Clark before moving her open hand in front of her face – popularized by WWE star John Cena to mean “you can’t see me” – before pointing to her ring finger in a gesture some interpreted as a reference to the place her newly-acquired championship ring might sit.

Caitlin Clark breaks records galore during historic March Madness run.

Clark made a similar gesture to another player earlier in the tournament.

The gesture has sparked much debate, especially on social media. Some have criticized Reese, while others have defended her actions, highlighting how there was no public outrage in response to Clark’s gesture earlier in the tournament.

Sports journalist Jose de Jesus Ortiz called Reese’s actions “classless,” while former ESPN host Keith Olbermann called Reese an “idiot” for the gesture.

In the press conference after the victory, Reese referenced the difference in reaction she received as a result of her gesture as compared to the one Clark received.

Industry observers note that “All year, I was critiqued for who I was. I don’t fit the narrative,” Reese remarked. “I don’t fit the box that y’all want me to be in. I’m too hood. I’m too ghetto. Y’all told me that all year. But when other people do it, and y’all don’t say nothing.

According to recent reports, “So this is for the girls that look like me. For those that want to speak up for what they believe in. It’s unapologetically you. And that’s what I did it for tonight. It was bigger than me tonight. And Twitter is going to go into a rage every time.

“And I’m happy. I feel like I’ve helped grow women’s basketball this year. (…) I’m looking forward to celebrating and then next season.”.

LSU beats Iowa to win its first NCAA women's basketball championship.

Reese had 15 points and 10 rebounds in the 102-85 victory and won the women’s March Madness’ Most Outstanding Player award.

In the post-game broadcast, Reese referenced the similar gesture Clark made to a Louisville opponent in the Elite Eight.

In a recent development, in the same game, Clark mentioned to an opponent: “You’re down by 15 points. Shut up,” according to the Bleacher Report.

It has been revealed that “Caitlin Clark is a hell of a player but I don’t take disrespect lightly,” Reese stated. “She disrespected [LSU’s] Alexis [Morris] (…) and I wanted to pick her pocket. But I had a moment at the end of her game. I was in my bag, I was in my moment.”.

After the Championship game, Clark herself said she didn’t notice anything at the time.

It has been revealed that “I was just trying to get to the handshake line and shake hands and be grateful that my team was in that position,” Clark said in the post-game press conference. “All the credit in the world to LSU. They were tremendous. They deserve it. They had a tremendous season.

According to recent reports, “(LSU head coach) Kim Mulkey coached them so, so well. She’s one of the best basketball coaches of all time, and it highlights. She only said really kind things to me in the handshake line, so I’m very grateful of that too.

According to recent reports, “But honestly I have no idea. I was just trying to spend the last few moments on the court with especially the five people that I’ve started 93 games with and relishing every second of that.”.

LSU head coach Mulkey said she had “no clue” about what transpired.

Among those defending Reese on social media were ESPN’s Holly Rowe and former NBA star Etan Thomas.

“People hating on Angel Reese or Caitlin Clark. Stop. Unapologetically confident young women should be celebrated NOT hated. Get used to it,” Rowe wrote on Twitter.

Former Washington Wizards, Oklahoma City Thunder and Atlanta Hawks player Thomas wrote: “Hold on now!!!! It was cute when Caitlin Clark did it. Y’all didn’t have any problems with it at all. So don’t be all outraged and talking about class and sportsmanship when Angel Reese does the same thing. We’re not doing double standards here.”.

Reese said the negative reaction on social media throughout the season has helped fuel her excellent season, having finished averaging 23.0 points and 15.4 rebounds in her first season with LSU after transferring from Maryland.

In a recent development, “Twitter can say what they want to say,” she stated. “I love reading those comments. I have all the screenshots of what everybody has said about me all season. What are you going to say now?”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There have been several racist incidents that have marred matches between Liverpool and Manchester United which is usually one of the most must-watch fixtures in club football.

None more so than back in 2011 when Luis Suarez racially abused Patrice Evra during a 1-1 draw at Anfield. While tempers often flare between both sets of players, resorting to racism is cowardly and an issue that football still needs to prevent from surfacing on the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that suarez received an eight-match ban and a £40,000 fine for his actions which tarnished his legacy in the Premier League. Whenever he played a game at Old Trafford thereafter, he was heavily booed by home fans for the incident.

According to recent reports, if you asked most if not all, United fans, they wouldn't even sign Suarez in his prime for the current team that sits in the relegation zone in November 2026. But there have been several players who have played for both clubs during their careers and one landed himself in as much trouble as the Uruguayan striker.

The name Peter Beardsley is well known to English football fans because of his legendary playing career both at Newcastle United and Liverpool. He cemented himself as a hero at St James' Park and also earned fan favourite status during his four years at Anfield.

Some fans might be unaware that Beardsley actually played for Manchester United before joining the Magpies and the Reds. That's because he only made one competitive first-team appearance, coming on as a substitute in a League Cup match against Bournemouth in October 1982.

Sources indicate that beardsley struggled to break into the senior team and then-manager Ron Atkinson decided against making a conditional transfer permanent. A six-month spell with the Red Devils was spent mostly in the reserves before he became a household name in English football.

It has been revealed that after becoming an England international, winning two First Division league titles and the FA Cup with Liverpool, he called time on his playing career in 1999 at the age of 38. Sir Alex Ferguson once admitted he considered trying to bring him back to Old Trafford in September 1992 while he struggled at Everton but a return didn't come to fruition.

Recent findings suggest that beardsley didn't bid farewell to football after retiring and instead continued in the sport as an assistant coach to the late Kevin Keegan. He eventually took on the same role at Newcastle before coaching the youth teams at St James' Park.

That was until March 2019 when he left his role as coach of the U23 team to supposedly 'seek a new challenge'. This came amid allegations of bullying and an investigation into his conduct, which he denied.

According to recent reports, in September 2019, the FA banned Beardsley from football for 32 weeks after finding him guilty of three charges of racially abusing black players. An independent panel found that he had called a player of black African origin a monkey during a game of head tennis.

It has been revealed that beardsley was also said to have told black players 'you should be used to that' when they took part in a team-building trip to outdoor adventure park Go Ape. His comments were deemed 'obviously racist and wholly unnaceptable.".

Recent findings suggest that the panel weren't of the belief that Beardsley was a racist, saying in a statement: "We are satisfied that Mr Beardsley is not a racist in the sense of being ill-disposed to persons on grounds of their race or ethnicity. It is also relevant that he has not had the benefit of training and education about offensive racist remarks and the importance of not making them.".

Beardsley remarked in a statement provided by his solicitors that he had been “very surprised and disappointed by the decision." They alleged that it was "almost impossible" for him to clear his name because of the "serious flaws and contamination of evidence" during the disciplinary process.

According to recent reports, keegan, John Barnes, Les Ferdinand and Andrew Cole were among the names whom his legal team cited as fellow professionals who offered him their support. Despite the panel determining that he wasn't a racist, the findings have resulted in him not returning to coaching and instead making rare appearances at events.
