Why Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch face a fight for their Liverpool futures under Andoni Iraola

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1398 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fourfourtwo

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Eighteen months ago, on his first return to Merseyside since leaving the club as manager the summer before, Jurgen Klopp spoke at a charity event at Liverpool Cathedral and singled out Dominik Szoboszlai for praise.
  • Probably the “best pressing player in Europe right now” was how the German described the Reds’ midfielder, who had played the season in the No.
  • Only nine months ago, Slot described the Hungarian as “maybe the best in the world in terms of pressing.” It’s quite the difference to today, when Szoboszlai’s pressing, now in a deeper role in midfield for Andoni Iraola, is coming into question.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eighteen months ago, on his first return to Merseyside since leaving the club as manager the summer before, Jurgen Klopp spoke at a charity event at Liverpool Cathedral and singled out Dominik Szoboszlai for praise.

Probably the “best pressing player in Europe right now” was how the German described the Reds’ midfielder, who had played the season in the No. 10 role as Arne Slot’s side swept to the title.

Only nine months ago, Slot described the Hungarian as “maybe the best in the world in terms of pressing.” It’s quite the difference to today, when Szoboszlai’s pressing, now in a deeper role in midfield for Andoni Iraola, is coming into question.

“I think, for me, it’s about, in his mind, managing how much he presses and when to go, as opposed to just pressing for pressing’s sake,” Daniel Sturridge explained during Sky Sports' coverage of the 3-1 win over Crystal Palace.

“I’m not saying that he does that all the time, but I think the reason why Liverpool are open is because they don’t have someone who’s reading in front of the defence.”.

That title-winning campaign two seasons ago saw Szoboszlai vital to everything Liverpool did well, with Alexis Mac Allister and Ryan Gravenberch complementing each other - everything was seemingly perfectly balanced. Gravenberch played in a more restricted No. 6 role in front of defence, Mac Allister was the box-to-box No. 8, and Szoboszlai was the all-action, pressing No. 10.

However, Slot worried that opponents had found out how to play against his team, and perhaps aware of losing Trent Alexander-Arnold’s unique creativity from deep, opted for a changed midfield set up. It actually began in the final away game of the title-winning season, away to Brighton, when Szoboszlai started in a two-man midfield alongside Gravenberch.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

According to recent reports, and that’s how Slot continued the following campaign, having signed Florian Wirtz for the No. 10 role. It was a move that immediately had its sceptics. Promising Wirtz the central role, where he had never truly played before, seemed to leave Liverpool far more open in midfield.

Szoboszlai, though, became the first Liverpool midfielder since Steven Gerrard to score and assist 10 or more goals in a single campaign, scoring 13 and assisting 12 in 53 games across all competitions. He was named the Reds’ player of the season.

That, though, doesn’t tell the full story. Some fans were irked by the Hungarian’s manner, especially after a heavy defeat at Manchester City. The match-going supporter noticed how often he slowed play down and often encouraged others to do so. Slot saw it differently, saying: “He is an all-round player, an all-round midfielder, a modern midfielder in my opinion. I think this season he has improved his game on the ball. Off the ball, he is top three, four or five in the world.”.

With two years left to run on his contract, Szoboszlai was rewarded for his form with a upcoming contract and named one of Iraola’s new vice-captains following the departures of Andy Robertson and Mohamed Salah. Szoboszlai’s importance to the club could not have been clearer, and for many he was - and is - regarded as the most likely captain-in-waiting after Virgil van Dijk departs, whether that’s next summer or later.

But 10 league games into the new season and it’s clear that Mac Allister is Iraola’s first-choice pick in his midfield two, and there are now growing calls for Trey Nyoni to be the player alongside the Argentine.

The pairing of Gravenberch and Szoboszlai was woefully exposed on the opening day at Newcastle, with the Dutchman finding himself very much out of favour once Mac Allister was back available after his later return due to the World Cup. But Mac Allister and Szoboszlai together also appears to lack balance, or understanding of when to press in Iraola’s system. “Both of the midfielders, whether it’s Mac Allister or Szoboszlai, have a tendency to vacate that space in front of the defence because of the press the manager wants to do,” Sturridge noted, accurately.

It has been revealed that injury to Szoboszlai during the last international break opened the door for teenager Nyoni's big break, including his first league start against Arsenal and his first time starting three consecutive matches. The reviews have been unanimous. The player who was handed his debut by Klopp at 16 has mightily impressed.

Nyoni’s first thought is always to play forward, capable of playing quick, direct passes into the attackers and splitting midfield in doing so. Some supporters see this as a stark contrast to Szoboszlai, who often runs with the ball or slows play and opts for a less positive pass.

According to recent reports, nyoni is also impressing off the ball, adept at tackling and comfortable dropping into the defensive line to start attacks from deep. The youngster explained Iraola’s instructions recently as being “as soon as you get the ball, it’s just play forward.”.

According to recent reports, “Trey is very good on the ball, very calm, he reads the situations well,” Iraola praised in pre-season. “We’re forcing him in the work without the ball, in the press, and he is absolutely doing very well. I think the timings of the jumps are very good. He is always confident on the ball so we encourage him.”.

The new boss is clearly a huge fan of the player, who was the subject of a late £30 million bid from Nottingham Forest in the summer and who fellow teenage prodigy Rio Ngumoha notes “definitely still has another level to go. You guys haven’t even seen him at his top, top level.”.

Sources indicate that on the bench for the Palace game, having started the previous three in a row - including away to Fenerbahce where he bagged his first goal - Nyoni’s involvement in Liverpool's third as sub at Selhurst Park underlined exactly what his strengths are. He read the pass from Tyrick Mitchell inside his own box, intercepting with his left foot, before looking up and immediately playing a quick ball out to Alexander Isak with his right foot that completely split the Palace midfield and started the attack that ended with the Swede pulling the trigger.

Two touches was all it took from Nyoni. Technically, it was superb; the vision and execution perfect. It had some supporters making comparisons to Fabinho or Thiago. There is an argument that Nyoni’s passing style gets more from all the forwards, who clearly benefit when they receive the ball rapidly, rather than once opposition defences have been able to get back behind the ball.

Liverpool have struggled against so-called low blocks for the past 18 months, since losing the qualities of a certain Alexander-Arnold (and more recently Salah) - Nyoni offers a much-needed solution to the creative dearth.

That, though, leaves a huge question of Szoboszlai - and Gravenberch, with both having signed newly introduced contracts this year.

“When a young player in midfield is playing ahead of them, that causes a problem,” Jamie Carragher expressed last week. “Basically, about where you’ve spent your money. It means you haven’t spent your money well enough.”.

Throw in reports of Liverpool’s interest in Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara, whose late move to Chelsea was scuppered on deadline day, and the picture becomes further complicated.

Will Nyoni’s emergence as a genuine option lead Liverpool to quell their interest in the Senegalese? And what to be done with Szoboszlai and Gravenberch if so? It can’t be as simple as selling two of the highest earners, but then you also can’t have two of your highest earners on the bench, either. The midfield conundrum could define Iraola’s first season, and it might lead to a high-profile departure or two.

Russia is back in world sport, but who is drug testing its athletes?

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (888 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fresh questions have emerged over Russia's return to world sport after figures reviewed by DW showed that only four of the 16 Russian weightlifters competing at this year's world championships underwent out-of-competition testing by the International Testing Agency (ITA).
  • Two-time European champion Anastasiia Romanova, who previously served a two-year doping ban, was among those not tested by the ITA during the first nine months of 2026, according to its quarterly anti-doping reports.
  • Recent findings suggest that by comparison, all 13 members of the North Korean team underwent at least one ITA test during the same period.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fresh questions have emerged over Russia's return to world sport after figures reviewed by DW showed that only four of the 16 Russian weightlifters competing at this year's world championships underwent out-of-competition testing by the International Testing Agency (ITA).

Two-time European champion Anastasiia Romanova, who previously served a two-year doping ban, was among those not tested by the ITA during the first nine months of 2026, according to its quarterly anti-doping reports.

Recent findings suggest that by comparison, all 13 members of the North Korean team underwent at least one ITA test during the same period. North Korea, like Russia, has a history of doping violations in weightlifting.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The ITA, which runs weightlifting's anti-doping program, told DW that it tested all 16 Russian weightlifters "ahead of their participation in the event." DW understands those tests were conducted in Ningbo, China, where the championships are being held.

In a recent development, in a power sport like weightlifting, performance-enhancing drugs are most beneficial during training, when athletes build strength and muscle mass in the months before competition. Some drugs, such as anabolic steroids, may be harder to detect by the time the competition comes around.

Rob Koehler, head of the athlete-led movement Global Athlete, called the lack of out-of-competition testing "absurd.".

It has been revealed that "Out-of-competition testing is the backbone of anti-doping," Koehler told DW. "Everybody knows there's going to be testing at the event. But not everybody knows when they're going to be tested 365 days a year outside events. It's concerning that the ITA doesn't see this as a red flag.".

Marta Nawrocka, the ITA's spokesperson, said that Russian athletes were among the 10 most-tested nationalities in weightlifting this year. She also defended the fact that only two Russian weightlifters feature in the sport's highest-priority testing pool, saying inclusion is based on performance and risk profiles.

Sources indicate that "Russia's history of doping in weightlifting remains an crucial factor in the ITA's risk assessment and testing priorities," Nawrocka mentioned. "Russian weightlifters remain subject to substantial testing activity.".

Koehler, though, is unconvinced.

It has been revealed that "You simply can't treat Russia like any other country," he noted. "It has to have more scrutiny. It has to have more testing. If you don't do that, you're undermining athlete confidence in the system.".

The International Weightlifting Federation did not respond to a request for comment.

Weightlifting was one of the sports most implicated in Russia's state-sponsored doping scandal, which came to light after the 2014 Sochi Winter Olympics. It ranked second only to athletics for the number of positive cases identified by Canadian lawyer Richard McLaren in his 2016 report commissioned by WADA, the global anti-doping watchdog.

The scandal led to dozens of Russian athletes being banned across numerous sports. RUSADA, Russia's anti-doping agency, has remained suspended for most of the past decade.

As a result, its Moscow laboratory cannot analyze urine and blood samples, meaning samples collected by the agency must be sent abroad for analysis under what WADA described as a "strict chain of custody.".

WADA stated it continued to monitor RUSADA but had been unable to gain access to the country to review the agency's suspension because of the "ongoing geopolitical situation.".

It added that RUSADA had "collected thousands of samples … including hundreds from weightlifters" so far this year.

Recent findings suggest that "Given the history, WADA remains vigilant when it comes to Russia," James Fitzgerald, WADA's spokesperson, told DW. "We must ensure that no stone is left unturned when it comes to verifying that all the proper testing and other anti-doping activities are taking place.".

Despite being suspended, RUSADA still has the power to investigate and prosecute anti-doping cases involving Russian athletes, which critics find difficult to reconcile.

"It's a compounding problem that WADA is still giving them a free pass when it can't even get into Russia to see what they're doing," stated Koehler, WADA's former deputy director general.

It has been revealed that "There's simply no oversight and no accountability. And quite frankly, I don't think there ever really has been.".

Critics also argue that ongoing questions over RUSADA's leadership and independence suggest that little has been fixed in the decade since the McLaren report.

Even the International Olympic Committee (IOC), whose president, Kirsty Coventry, supports the full return of Russian athletes, has acknowledged a "lack of confidence" over RUSADA's governance.

Nawrocka noted the IOC had "recently entrusted" the ITA with an expanded role within Russia in the run-up to the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028, but did not explain what the role would involve or when it might begin.

According to recent reports, in April, investigative outlet The Insider reported that Veronika Loginova, the agency's head, was in a long-term relationship with an alleged FSB officer. The FSB, Russia's domestic security service, played a central role in covering up positive drug tests at the Sochi Games.

Loginova did not respond to questions for this article but dismissed the allegations at the time as "all this nonsense," writing in an email that she believed "sport exists separate from politics.".

WADA confirmed to DW only that its investigations unit was examining the allegations against Loginova and that the inquiry was ongoing.

The England back row, never knowingly far from controversy, escalated a brawl at the end of the first half that Leicester prop Joe Heyes revealed “added fuel to the fire” of a Tigers side who roared impressively when they returned after the break.

Pollock, withdrawn after 52 minutes, may wish to reflect on the wisdom of riling the Tigers in their own lair.

“That was a proper Tigers second half and a really pleasing performance,” Geoff Parling, their director of rugby, said.

It has been revealed that “We got on the front foot and showed our power. The way the guys problem-solved was brilliant and I’m just really pleased with the emotional energy they threw into that game.

“The way we were physically for each other – I’m really pleased.

“The challenge for us, if we want to be a title-winning team, is to play like that when it isn’t Northampton Saints. We have to play with that heart – the fire we showed in our chests – but also the calmness we showed too.

“I think if we play our game to the best of our ability we can knock over anyone.”.

It’s a big day for Alex Coles, who celebrates his milestone 150th cap today.

The 27-year-old lock follows Fraser Dingwall, Rory Hutchinson and Alex Mitchell to become the fourth member of Saints’ current squad to reach 150 appearances for his boyhood club, eight years after making his debut in 2018.

Coles marks one of nine changes to Saints’ side for the Derby Day clash, with Emmanuel Iyogun, Curtis Langdon, Ed Prowse, Tom Pearson and Henry Pollock the other names coming into the forward pack.

Cleopas Kundiona retains his place in the front row while milestone man Coles joins Prowse in the second row against Tigers.

Josh Kemeny, with the 27-year-old continues at blindside flanker while Tom Pearson is set to make his first Prem appearance of the season.

Northampton Saints: J Pater; T Freeman, R Hutchinson, F Dingwall, G Hendy; F Smith, A Mitchell, E Iyogun, C Langdon, C Kundiona, A Coles, E Prowse, J Kemeny, T Pearson, H Pollock.

Replacements: R Smith, D Fischetti, I Neculai, JJ Van Der Mescht, T Lockett, C Chick, A McParland, O Sleightholme.

Parling has made five changes from the side that endured a 41-17 defeat to Pau.

Solomone Kata returns from injury to start at inside centre, with Gabriel Hamer-Webb and Jack van Poortvliet also coming into the backline to replace Ollie Hassell-Collins and Tom Whiteley respectively.

In the pack, Joe Heyes joins Archie van der Flier and Jamie Blamire who retain their places in the front row, while the second row make up of Cameron Henderson and Ollie Chessum remains unchanged.

Aaron Wainwright comes back into the starting lineup in the back row, with Finn Carnduff moving to openside flanker, with Olly Cracknell going at No 8.

Leicester: F Steward; A Radwan, W Wand, S Kata; G Hamer-Webb; B Searle, J van Poortvliet; A van der Flier, J Blamire, J Heyes, C Henderson, O Chessum, A Wainwright, F Carnduff, O Cracknell.

Replacements:  R Asiata, T Haffar, W Hurd, J Thompson, J Moro, T Whiteley, O Bailey, G Pearson.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the upcoming campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Industry observers note that tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” said Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”.

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”.

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Industry observers note that kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

Paris Saint-Germain fear Désiré Doue has suffered a serious knee injury, a fresh blow for Luis Enrique days before Roma visit the Parc des Princes in the Champions League.

According to Foot Mercato, the 21-year-old’s right knee gave way while he was shielding the ball, with no contact from an opponent, late in the first half of Saturday’s Ligue 1 game at Nice. He had scored to make it 2-1 only minutes earlier.

In a recent development, doué left the pitch in tears on a stretcher and was replaced by Ferran Torres. PSG are waiting for scans to confirm how serious the injury is, but Foot01 report that the club fear a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament.

According to recent reports, if confirmed, it would be a second major knee injury in barely a month for the European champions. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia ruptured the ACL in his right knee in October’s 4-2 win over Barcelona and is expected to miss most of the season. Ousmane Dembélé and Marquinhos also suffered thigh injuries in that game.

Doué had only just returned from an earlier injury when he joined up with France this month.

Sources indicate that PSG are chasing a third consecutive Champions League title, and they host Gian Piero Gasperini’s Roma on Wednesday at 21:00 CET [20:00 GMT]. Whatever the scans show, Doué is very unlikely to face the Giallorossi.

  • Sources indicate that musiala's long-term health has become an matter for Bayern, who have publicly and internally debated whether the German can return to his best.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rio Ferdinand has weighed in on the controversy surrounding Bayern Munich's handling of Jamal Musiala after FIFPRO raised concerns over comments made by the club's hierarchy.

Sources indicate that musiala's long-term health has become an matter for Bayern, who have publicly and internally debated whether the German can return to his best. The young attacker collapsed during pre-season friendlies in the summer and has since confirmed he is managing a neurological dysfunction with medication.

The 23-year-old's health complications have prevented him from playing regularly so far this season, limiting him to five appearances. He returned from a torn muscle fiber that had sidelined him for around two months when he came off the bench in Friday's 1-1 draw against FC Koln.

Musiala's long-term future in football became the subject of intense speculation, with rumours circulating online about a potential imminent retirement. Those claims were proven untrue, but Bayern's higher-ups have still voiced concerns over whether he can recapture the form he highlighted prior to his illness.

Industry observers note that supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge received huge criticism for his comments on the situation. He suggested that the club would be within their rights to question his contract if they felt 'what he’s capable of now isn’t what’s stipulated in the contract.'.

According to recent reports, those comments came after honorary president Uli Hoeneß described Musiala's illness as "not easily curable" and a dilemma for the Bundesliga outfit. At the club's Annual General Meeting on Saturday, CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen and club president Herbert Hainer confirmed Bayern were unaware of Musiala's condition when signing him to an extension until 2030.

Dreesen and Hainer both denied feeling misled by the player's camp over the new deal, which runs until 2030. FIFPRO have now condemned those remarks in a statement criticizing the club's treatment of the player.

In stated statement, FIFPRO stated that they are "deeply concerned by the repeated public statements from Bayern Munich's leadership calling into question the contract of Jamal Musiala as he returns from injury.".

In a recent development, they added: "Bayern’s honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala’s contract in quick succession. In FIFPRO’s view, this is a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern’s standing should know better.".

Sources indicate that "Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala. Across professional football, uncertainty about a player’s future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury. Making Musiala’s health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.".

FIFPRO pointed out that a player's form or an injury does not give a club ground to reopen terms it agreed to: "Clubs, leagues and player unions have agreed at FIFA level that contractual stability is a core principle of the game. It protects clubs as much as it protects players.".

Former Manchester United defender Ferdinand agreed with FIFPRO's stance, in which the players' union also spoke of standing with Musiala and all players who "honour their commitments." He shared his thoughts on Bayern's handling of the Germany international's condition and contract by highlighting player welfare:.

"Bayern Munich are better than this.... if they want to negotiate more reasonable terms for the club going forward due to the health problems Jamal has, then surely speak to him and his team rather than to the media.

He added: "This situation must be hard enough to deal with for Jamal without the media and club officials talking about it publicly. Bayern Munich are one of the clubs who from afar have always carried themselves with a class and standard that most have admired. Sadly, this just doesn't feel like Bayern Munich in this situation.".

Musiala has been at Bayern since 2019 when he joined the club's youth academy from Chelsea. He became the youngest goalscorer in their history at the age of 17 and 205 days before helping the Bavarians win six Bundesliga titles, the Champions League and the DFB-Pokal.

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill hailed midfield duo Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan after the recalled pair both scored in the 4-1 home win over St Mirren.

With Mika Baur facing 10 weeks out with an ankle injury and Benjamin Nygren nursing a heel problem, O’Neill handed McCowan his second start of the season and Oxlade-Chamberlain his fifth, as the two joined forces for the first time.

Oxlade-Chamberlain and McCowan netted either side of Camilo Duran in a nine-minute flurry of goals late in the first half with Callum McGregor making it four for Celtic in the second period before Killian Phillips reduced the deficit for Saints from the penalty spot.

It has been revealed that O’Neill said: ‘Alex has been waiting around for a while to get into the side. He’s a brilliant passer of the ball. He took his goal very well with a calm finish in the bottom corner.

‘He was feeling a little bit sore, so taking him off was just precautionary.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I was also delighted Luke got his goal. That should give him a boost in confidence.’.

Oxlade-Chamberlain congratulates McCowan after he scored to make it three for Celtic.

McCowan faced criticism after Celtic’s Champions League collapse against LASK and his only previous start this season saw him taken off at half-time in a home defeat by Rangers.

O’Neill stated: ‘I thought he did really well, also playing the full game given it has been some considerable time since he has done that.

Industry observers note that ‘He got the ball early on and played it almost blindly and it was intercepted and I thought, “oh, gosh, here we go”. But he roared back, took his goal well and I am really pleased for him. He is a real genuine lad.

It has been revealed that ‘It has been tough for him. In the game against Rangers, he was thrown into a position, and it didn’t start well for him in the match. I think he felt it was deja vu for him in terms of the game at the back end of last season too. That will be good for him.’.

The Celtic manager also introduced 19-year-old former PSV Eindhoven midfielder Joel van den Berg for a debut in the second half.

Industry observers note that ‘I thought he did very well,’ remarked O’Neill. ‘He’s coming on after an injury which kept him out for some time.

‘I am pleased there is a bit of competition for places now.’.

The veteran midfielder celebrates his strike that opened the scoring against St Mirren.

St Mirren manager Craig McLeish felt Celtic were clinical in his team’s heavy defeat in Glasgow.

‘It’s a really sore one with the way the scoreline ended up,’ noted McLeish.

It has been revealed that ‘I thought we started the game quite well and then that flurry of goals can happen here when you’re playing against such a strong team. The difference was the quality in our box compared to theirs.

‘They are just so clinical, and they get into those good areas and they punish you.

‘I felt we got into some similar areas throughout the game. We didn’t give up, we didn’t move away from what we were trying to do, but we were just really lacking that final bit.’.

Arsenal legend Ian Wright indicates he found it “worrying” how the Gunners seemed to collapse today against Newcastle United in a similar way to their 3-0 defeat against Brighton earlier this season.

Mikel Arteta’s side have mostly been in superb form this season, and they remain six points clear of Manchester City as things stand, even if they will undoubtedly be disappointed to have dropped points away to Newcastle today.

Arsenal took the lead in the first half and looked like potentially running away with it after a dominant display, but then Newcastle stunned them with a quickfire double in the second half.

Noni Madueke managed to equalise for the visitors, but Wright was a bit concerned with some elements of what he saw….

"It was a bit worrying to see Arsenal collapse like they did".

Industry observers note that ian Wright shares his full-time thoughts as Arsenal draw 2-2 with Newcastle at St James' Park ? pic.twitter.com/Z8olpBf9q4.

— Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) November 21, 2026.

According to recent reports, speaking after the game, Wright told Sky Sports: “It reminded me of Arsenal against Brighton. They couldn’t see it off against Brighton, and obviously we lost.

“But Newcastle, they had a spell when they were doing the same thing … it was a bit worrying to see Arsenal collapse like they did for the time that they did.”.

It certainly wasn’t a vintage Arsenal performance for a decent chunk of that second half, with the north London giants looking uncharacteristically suspect at the back.

Arsenal’s players will surely have been aware of Man City dropping points earlier today with their 1-1 draw at home to Fulham.

This meant AFC could have gone eight points clear of Enzo Maresca’s side with a win at St James’ Park, and that would have left their title rivals with a real mountain to climb.

As it is, this title race is still pretty open, though of course City have the 115 charges hanging over their heads, which could lead to a hefty points deduction at some point later on in the campaign.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European shares fell sharply in early trading on Friday as a global sell-off fueled by concerns over artificial intelligence stocks spread from Wall Street to Asia and Europe.

Fears of curbs on AI data-center spending have added to investors' concerns after Democrats won control of both chambers of the US Congress.

Recent findings suggest that the pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 1.6% in early trading, wiping out its gains for the week. Most major European markets fell more than 1%, with media, healthcare and retail stocks leading the declines.

European markets had previously weathered the week's turbulence better than their Asian and US counterparts because of their more limited exposure to AI stocks.

Earlier, Japanese and South Korean shares tumbled after a massive selloff in tech stocks on Wall Street the previous day.

It has been revealed that tokyo's benchmark Nikkei 225 index fell 5.5% in early trade, while Seoul's tech-heavy Kospi index slid as much as 8.8%, triggering a circuit breaker which suspended trading for 20 minutes. Taiwan's benchmark TAIEX index was also down more than 8%.

Asian tech giants including Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) have borne the brunt of the artificial intelligence-related selloff.

Samsung plunged nearly 10% while SK Hynix slid over 11%.

Chip-related shares in Japan also took a beating, with Tokyo Electron stock trading down around 9% and Kioxia shedding 13%.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US markets were hammered on Thursday by a sharp retreat in tech stocks, particularly those involved in the buildout of artificial intelligence infrastructure like data centers.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 5.52% and shed as much as $2.5 trillion (roughly €2.23 trillion) in market value, while the broader S&P 500 index plunged 4.4%.

The rout occurred as investors grow increasingly anxious about the colossal AI spending prepares and whether they will eventually produce commensurate profits.

The results of the US midterm elections, which saw Democrats seize control of both houses of US Congress, added to the concerns.

A number of Democratic governors-elect campaigned on slowing artificial intelligence development and promised to stop or pause the construction of data centers amid growing public opposition to such projects.

"It's pretty clear there's been a real shift ​in sentiment," Michael McCarthy, chief executive for Australia and Newly introduced Zealand at online brokerage Moomoo, told the Reuters news agency.

According to recent reports, "Market turning points are often accompanied by strong disagreement, and that indicates up in the market ​by huge swings in either direction," he stated. "That's what we appear to have had — and last night's emphatic sell-down suggests that is the direction that we're now headed in.".

Manchester United are open to bringing Scott McTominay back to the club in a shock move, according to a report, with their chances of actually re-signing the Scotland international revealed.

Man United chiefs are ready to back latest manager Mauricio Pochettino in the transfer market, and as soon as the January transfer window, in order to help him turn the club's fortunes around.

The Red Devils go into the Argentine head coach's first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday 19th in the standings, after Sunderland leapfrogged them on Saturday with their draw against Aston Villa.

Pochettino knows that a draw at Anfield will be enough to take them out of the bottom three, and that must be the minimum aim as he looks to lead the club up the table.

The 54-year-old must work with the current squad of players for the next six weeks before the January window opens, but it is expected that new players will be brought to Old Trafford in the New Year.

GIVEMESPORT sources have revealed that the club are looking at some key positions ahead of January, including the centre-back and striker positions, as well as both full-back positions.

The former two appear to be the priority, with GMS understanding that Fulham's Calvin Bassey is appreciated by the club, and he is able to play as both a left-sided centre-half and a left-back.

When Man United Signed First-Choice Defence.

United are also keen on his Cottagers' team-mate Antonee Robinson, while Folarin Balogun is another United States international linked with a move to Old Trafford, given the success he has had under Pochettino at international level, and the fact that Monaco are willing to sell.

A move for Chelsea right-back Malo Gusto could also be 'one to watch', according to GMS sources.

Fabrizio Romano expects the club to look at a new centre-back and striker in January too, but it would be a shock if they looked at a new midfielder given they signed three at a cost of more than £150m in the summer.

Still, TEAMtalk claim that the club has been offered the chance to re-sign McTominay from Napoli, and they are refusing to rule out sanctioning a deal.

Despite winning the Serie A title in his first season at the club, and being named as the MVP of the league at the same time, the Scotland international's future in Naples is in doubt.

There are just 18 months left on the 29-year-old's contract at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, and with no breakthrough in negotiations, an exit is looking increasingly likely.

McTominay made the decision to leave Old Trafford in 2024, but the report claims that he is now ready to explore a return to England and the Premier League, should he fail to reach an agreement to stay at Napoli.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that homo erectus might have also lived in rainforests — previously thought to be a habitat in which only modern humans could have thrived.Credit: S. Entressangle/E. Daynes/SPL.

Homo erectus is already one of humans’ most extraordinary ancient relatives. The major-brained, tool-wielding species emerged two million years ago in Africa and expanded across Eurasia, before vanishing around 100,000 years ago in Java, Indonesia.

Did Homo erectus and Denisovans mate? Tooth proteins hint at ancient trysts.

Did Homo erectus and Denisovans mate? Tooth proteins hint at ancient trysts.

Researchers have now added another feather to the hominin’s cap. A pair of studies analysing fossil teeth1,2, which were published in Nature on 18 November, suggest that H. erectus thrived in dense rainforests in southern China as recently as 180,000 years ago.

Recent findings suggest that researchers had thought that H. erectus was limited to savannahs and open woodlands, says Kira Westaway, a geochronologist at Macquarie University in Sydney, Australia, and a co-author of both studies.

Recent findings suggest that “Never, ever have we seen them in rainforests,” she adds. “This is a really substantial deal, because we thought Homo sapiens were the only species that had the skill set to survive in really challenging rainforest environments.”.

The earliest H. erectus fossils, from eastern Africa, are 1.9 million years old. But the svelte, upright-walking and running hominins wasted little time, reaching western Asia and present-day China some 200,000 years later and modern Java, using land bridges, not long after. The last-known H. erectus remains, from central Java, date to roughly 110,000 years ago3.

Limestone caves in Guangxi province, southern China, contained more than 10,000 fossil teeth.Credit: Kira Westaway (Macquarie University).

It has been revealed that while looking for fossils from a three-metre-tall great ape called Gigantopithecus, Westaway and her colleagues identified a pair of limestone caves in Guangxi province in southern China. There, they discovered more than 10,000 fossil teeth from animals such as orangutans (Pongo spp.), monkeys and wild boar (Sus spp.), as well as 9 from hominins. The researchers estimate that the hominins lived between 184,000 and 324,000 years ago, according to dating of both fossils and the surrounding sediments using various methods.

Sources indicate that eight of the hominin teeth resembled those of H. erectus in their shape, a designation that was confirmed by analysing the sequences of proteins preserved in the dental enamel of four specimens, says co-author Frido Welker, a molecular palaeoanthropologist at the University of Copenhagen.

The tooth enamel was analysed and its proteins sequenced.Credit: Kira Westaway (Macquarie University).

The ninth lacked the shape and protein signature of H. erectus teeth, claims Welker, and it also didn’t resemble those of H. sapiens or Neanderthals (Homo neanderthalensis). Denisovans — enigmatic ancient humans first discovered in southern Siberia and now linked to diverse fossils from China and elsewhere in Asia — are a possibility, but the evidence is circumstantial, says Welker. “Every label we put on that ninth tooth is a little bit of speculation.”.

According to recent reports, the multitude of animal teeth was probably accumulated by a scavenger such as a porcupine. The presence of fossils from species such as muntjac deer (Muntiacus muntjac), leopards and orangutans hints at a rainforest environment.

In a recent development, for a number of years, Wayne Rooney was among the very best players in the Premier League. He won the competition five times at Manchester United and lifted many more major honours under Sir Alex Ferguson.

Recent findings suggest that he also established himself as one of the greatest English footballers of all time, scoring a then-record 53 international goals with the Three Lions. But it all started for the footballer at Everton.

Industry observers note that still just 16 years old, Rooney declared himself to the world with a stunning strike against Arsenal, which instantly went down in Premier League folklore. He played a total of 117 times for the Toffees, across two spells, starring alongside club icons such as Duncan Ferguson, Leighton Baines, and Kevin Campbell.

One of his former teammates, however, retired in 2011 and is now in jail.

Li Tie was a defensive midfielder who started out in China at Liaoning FC before being picked up by Everton in 2002. After an initial loan, he signed permanently and went on to play 40 times for the Toffees, with 30 appearances coming alongside Rooney.

Former teammate David Unsworth once stated:.

“He was tidy on the ball, skilful, he fitted right in. He didn’t try and segregate himself as a foreign player, he enjoyed the banter and had a laugh. He was an absolute diamond of a bloke.”.

Li left Goodison Park in 2006, but stayed in England for two more seasons, playing just once for Sheffield United due to an injury. He then returned to China, playing for Chengdu Blades and Liaoning Whowin before retiring in 2011. Sadly, injury problems were to blame again.

According to recent reports, despite his fitness struggles across his career, he still played 92 times for his country, making him China's 11th-most-capped men's player in history. After hanging up his boots, he later got into coaching, but this is where his troubles started.

After spells in charge of Hebei China Fortune and Wuhan Zall, Li served asinterim manager from 2019, taking over from Marcello Lippi, before being appointed permanently in 2020 and leaving the post in 2021.

A year after he left his post, China’s public prosecutor put out a bombshell statement which accused Li of ‘accepting and offering bribes’ to an array of individuals, including non-state employees:.

"Li Tie, the former head coach of the Chinese national men’s football team, was suspected of accepting bribes, offering bribes, offering bribes at the unit, accepting bribes of non-state employees, and offering bribes to non-state employees.”.

According to recent reports, in 2024, he made a televised confession, admitting to the match-fixing despite knwiing that people found guilty and convicted of corruption in his country have been given long prison sentences. His statement read:.

Sources indicate that "I'm very sorry. I should have kept my head to the ground and followed the right path. There were certain things that at the time were common practices in football. By gaining 'success' through such improper means, it actually made me more and more impatient and eager for quick results.".

According to recent reports, he added: "In order to achieve good performance, I resorted to influencing referees, bribing opposing players and coaches, sometimes through clubs dealing with other clubs. This behaviour becomes a habit, and eventually, there is even a slight dependence on these practices.".

The former Everton player admittedhe paid £330,000 (3 million yuan) in bribes to become manager of the Chinese national team, and added that match-fixing was rife throughout his two promotions with Hebei China Fortune and Wuhan Zall.

In a recent development, A court in Hubei province alleged that from 2015, when he was an assistant coach at the Hebei China Fortune club, until 2021, when he quit as China coach, Li gave and received bribes totalling 120 million yuan ($16.5 million). In exchange for bribes, the court stated, Li would select certain individuals for the national team as well as help clubs win competitions and sign players.

His punishment was severe, as he was sentenced to 20 years in prison for giving and receiving bribes. Not only that, but in 2026, while still locked away, he was also given a lifetime ban by the Chinese Football Association for match-fixing.

Latest Update: Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1037 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In 2025, an international trial found that people treated for colon cancer were more likely to be alive eight years later if they had received long-term exercise coaching.
  • According to recent reports, the question facing doctors now is less whether people with cancer should exercise, and rather how they should build it into routine care.
  • Yet experts caution that the trial's findings may not apply to every cancer or every patient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 2025, an international trial found that people treated for colon cancer were more likely to be alive eight years later if they had received long-term exercise coaching.

According to recent reports, the question facing doctors now is less whether people with cancer should exercise, and rather how they should build it into routine care. In the US, that shift is reaching hospital standards. From January 2027, breast cancer centers must screen patients' physical function and recommend exercise or physical therapy where needed.

Yet experts caution that the trial's findings may not apply to every cancer or every patient.

The 2025 trial, called CHALLENGE, was led by the Canadian Cancer Trials Group. It began enrolling patients in 2009 and published its results in 2025.

The trial's 889 participants came from six countries, most from Canada and Australia. All had finished surgery and chemotherapy for stage 2 or 3 colon cancer, which had not spread to distant organs.

Half received only health education materials on exercise and healthy eating. The other half additionally met a physical activity consultant for three years.

It has been revealed that in the exercise group, the target was similar to adding 45 to 60 minutes of brisk walking, three to four times a week. The amount and type of activity varied from person to person, said Tormod Skogstad Nilsen, a cancer exercise researcher in Norway. But he said participants achieved lasting increases in their physical activity.

According to recent reports, exercise helped. People in the exercise group were less likely to see their cancer come back, to develop a new cancer or to die. In all, 93 had at least one of these setbacks, compared with 131 in the health education group.

In cancer research, living longer usually means a larger share of people is still alive at a given point. It does not promise anyone a set number of extra years.

According to recent reports, eight years after joining CHALLENGE, about 90 of every 100 people in the exercise group were alive, compared with about 83 of every 100 in the health education group. That is about 7% more people alive in the group who had guided exercise.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that for people without cancer, the evidence comes from studies that follow people's habits and health over many years. These can show a link, but not prove cause and effect. Active people may also eat better or smoke less.

According to recent reports, in another 2025 study, more than 85,000 adults in the United Kingdom wore a wrist tracker for a week. Over about six years, those who moved most had a 26% lower risk of 13 cancers, including breast and colorectal cancer, than those who moved least.

Industry observers note that even light activity, such as household chores, was linked to lower risk. The link held after researchers accounted for lifestyle, weight and other health conditions.

Earlier research, based on people's self-reporting, has led to similar conclusions. A 2016 analysis of 1.44 million adults in the US and Europe linked free-time activity to a lower risk of many cancers, largely regardless of weight or smoking.

A trial to prove prevention is unlikely: Many cancers take years to develop, so it would need huge numbers of people followed for a long time.

In a recent development, CHALLENGE included only people with colon cancer. But how it picked participants offers a clue: Before joining, they had to pass a fitness test.

Anna Campbell, a professor of clinical exercise science at Edinburgh Napier University in Scotland, sees that as a guide.

Recent findings suggest that "I think patients with any other cancer stage II and III who have a reasonable baseline level of fitness and no major comorbidities that would prevent them from undertaking moderate to vigorous activity could be considered for similar interventions," she mentioned. Comorbidities are other health conditions.

Nilsen noted some people decline to join exercise trials because they feel too unwell or tired, or do not want to exercise. "Hence, study populations are typically younger, 'healthier', and most times slightly more motivated compared to a clinical population," he mentioned.

The coaching aimed to make activity a lasting habit, and Campbell said that is where the trial's value lies.

"The main success of the study is that it enabled the participants to become independent exercisers staying active in a safe and effective and individualized way," she noted.

Nilsen agreed. Helping people become more active "in their own environment," without depending on a well-equipped training center, "would likely lead to more sustainable activity behavioral changes," he said.

According to recent reports, he is wary of fixed targets, however. "Exercise should be tailored to each individual and the challenges they face, rather than striving to reach a given minimum of exercise required," though health care resources may not always allow it, he added.

Industry observers note that in a 2024 survey of 549 people with cancer, only one in 10 had been referred to an exercise service. Yet almost three in four thought their oncologist should raise the subject.

In a recent development, "There are some excellent examples of effective pathways but these are few and far between," stated Campbell. Good services bring everyone on board, from surgeons to community fitness instructors.

"Ideally, one person in the clinical setting needs to champion the program to link all the team together.".

Industry observers note that campbell expects CHALLENGE's regular coaching will be cut back in everyday care. Apps and live online group sessions could still work, she said, if run by properly trained staff.

According to recent reports, one recent study of live online exercise engaged patients from poorer backgrounds, in rural areas and with advanced cancer. "It answered some of the barriers, such as cost, travel and lack of confidence," she noted.

Patients can ask their care team what exercise is safe for them and what support exists.

According to Nilsen, a training session can bring structure and company. "You made it here, despite your feeling unwell or fatigued this morning, so you feel mastery based on that," he stated.

Arsenal could be in trouble if David Raya’s injury is as bad as it looks, according to pundit Jamie Redknapp.

The Gunners drew 2-2 away to Newcastle United today and should arguably have done better after making such a strong start, but the biggest worry of all is surely the injury to Raya.

The Spanish shot-stopper has been a world class performer for Arsenal, playing a major part in their Premier League title success last season, with backup ‘keeper Kepa Arrizabalaga a long way from those high standards.

See below for Redknapp’s reaction at the end of today’s game, as he stated Raya is irreplaceable in this Arsenal side, and his absence for a lengthy period could be a “massive” blow for the club’s prospects this season….

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Donyell Malen bagged four goals to give Roma their 5-1 victory away to Parma, with Rodrigo Mora also on target, but Wesley was decisive too with a hand in four goals.

The Giallorossi received a massive boost with the return of Paulo Dybala and Mile Svilar, the goalkeeper after nearly two months out, with Manu Koné and Gianluca Mancini also recovered after missing international duty, leaving only Devyne Rensch and Lorenzo Pellegrini on the treatment table.

Sources indicate that the Ducali had shown improvement under coach Alberto Gilardino, but the early Abdoulaye Ndiaye red card saw them lose to Bologna. He was therefore suspended, with David Romero and Dominik Drobnic out, plus Diego Carlos and Adrian Bernabé not at 100 per cent.

See how it all unfolded on the Liveblog.

Mariano Troilo stung Svilar’s gloves at the near post in the opening 60 seconds, but a few minutes later the goalkeeper rushed out to gather a loose ball and was visibly struggling with a muscular twinge, although he insisted on staying on the field.

Koné went down far too easily when feeling Troilo’s hand on his shoulder, while Leonardo Balerdi threw himself in the path of an El Bilal Touré finish from 12 yards.

Defensive bodies were also important to stop Enrico Delprato turning in from six yards on an Emanuele Valeri cross, but on the resulting corner, Svilar made a sensational reaction save on the Giovanni Fabbian header from point-blank range.

Mario Hermoso blasted just over from the edge of the box, and Giovanni Daffara was brave off his line to smother a Dybala pass at the feet of Donyell Malen, getting a shinpad in the head for his trouble.

Recent findings suggest that roma did break the deadlock with a moment of pure class from Malen. He hooked the Emanuele Lulli cross out of the air with his back to goal, knocking it down so it was in the right place as he turned to sweep in from 10 yards.

Mancini and Touré got into an argument with some possible hair-pulling and arm-flailing, but on the stroke of half-time a desperate clearance prevented Malen meeting the Rodrigo Mora low cross from six yards.

Daffara flew to parry the Dybala effort after a Malrn back-heel flick, but just as Roma were pouring forward, they were beaten on the counter-attack.

Leonardo Balerdi felt that he had the loose ball under control, but Elphege flicked it away to sprint from the centre-circle and beat the on-rushing Svilar.

Daffara made a magnificent reaction save to push the Mancini header out from under the bar on a Roma corner, but Malen could not turn down the gift from Troilo.

The defender made a complete mess of trying to clear the Wesley cross from the right, so it bobbled into the path of the Dutchman to fire in from six yards.

Moments later, there was a very similar goal again prompted by substitute Wesley’s pull-back from the right, it took a deflection and Rodrigo Mora pounced to tap in from close range.

The introduction of Brazil international Wesley really was transformative, as he provided another assist, rolling across from the right for Malen to complete his hat-trick.

Matias Soulé tested Daffara from distance, as did Hans Nicolussi Caviglia at the other end with Svilar.

It wasn’t over, as Malen scored his fourth of the game when Wesley won it back in midfield and placed a perfectly-weighted pass to send him sprinting, took a touch to get around Daffara, and placed the finish into the tiny sliver of goal remaining as defenders scrambled back to cover.

Malen 39, 68, 77, 90 (R), Elphege 54 (P), Mora 71 (R).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

So much for Xabi Alonso’s call for cool heads from his Chelsea players. Cole Palmer lost his and was sent off, while goalkeeper Mike Penders punched the ball into his own net to give Tottenham Hotspur a helping hand on their way to a second win at Stamford Bridge in 42 attempts.

This was hardly “the Battle of the Bridge”, but Chelsea blew up during a ridiculous 10-minute spell towards the end of a game in which Tottenham had bossed possession but not looked like scoring.

Palmer was lucky to stay on the pitch in the 70th minute, when he shoved his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes after the Tottenham midfielder had stopped him racing through with a foul and a handball.

Christopher Kavanagh, the referee, let him off with a yellow card, but 10 minutes later Palmer inexplicably gave Kavanagh no choice but to book him again and send him off, following a late challenge on substitute Conor Gallagher.

"It's PETULANT from Cole Palmer...you have to take it on the chin" Jamie Redknapp and Daniel Sturridge react to Cole Palmer's pair of yellow cards 🟥 https://t.co/Voxoo3Ea7V.

Palmer was just about the only Chelsea player not to have been sent off last season, but it seems that Alonso has not yet managed to deal with the club’s disciplinary problem.

Jordan Henderson had given Palmer a talking to at the end of the win at Everton in which the forward was booked. But he evidently did not heed the advice or the words of his manager.

Alonso had noted he was confident his players could keep calm ahead of the game, but he got that wrong – along with his team selection and substitutions.

Recent findings suggest that in between Palmer’s two bookings, Penders suffered his own moment of madness with a bizarre own goal on his league debut for Chelsea. The Belgian was standing in for Emi Martinez, who watched in disbelief from the home dug-out after undergoing surgery on his jaw.

Recent findings suggest that fernandes sent in a corner that Jan Paul van Hecke challenged for. Penders looked like the easy winner in that contest, but he got his punch horribly wrong and the ball spun backwards and over the goalline.

Spurs have taken the lead after Mateus Fernandes' corner ends up in Chelsea's goal ⚽️ https://t.co/X65gyO9yPX.

A man and a goal down, Chelsea then saw hundreds of their own fans walk out when Mathys Tel scored a brilliant second for Spurs with three minutes remaining. The visiting fans, who had seen one win at the Bridge since 1990 prior to Saturday, could hardly believe what they had seen.

It has been revealed that "Just look what it means!" A glorious solo run and finish from Mathys Tel! 🤩 https://t.co/Qg7WMFNlwQ.

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi celebrated wildly with his staff. The two benches had clashed and De Zerbi had been booked after Palmer’s first yellow card that the Italian felt should have been a red. But De Zerbi will not care about that now, with Tottenham’s season finally up and running thanks to successive league wins against Coventry City and Chelsea.

"They were brilliant Spurs, they really were" Gary Neville's immediate reaction to Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham 🗣️ https://t.co/QWhi7Blmfz.

Tottenham should really have been ahead in the first half. De Zerbi revealed before the game that Dominic Solanke had dropped down to the substitutes’ bench because the striker “felt fatigue” after the victory over Coventry.

With Solanke resting up on the bench until the 65th minute, De Zerbi moved Omar Marmoush, who had scored his first Spurs goal against Coventry, into the middle and brought in Tel on the left.

It has been revealed that tel was involved in the 29th-minute move that should have resulted in the opening goal for Marmoush. The Frenchman played a one-two with Andy Robertson and the Scotsman picked out Marmoush with a low cross. But, six yards out and with time to pick his spot, the former Manchester City man allowed Penders to make a save.

The missed Marmoush chance was the first time Penders had been called into action. At the other end, Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky made unnecessary work for himself.

Kinsky played a bad pass straight to Pedro Neto. The ball was worked to Henderson, but Kinsky recovered to make a save and then stopped the follow-up from Neto. The offside flag then went up, but it was unclear whether it would have spared Kinsky on both occasions had Chelsea scored.

It was not the first time Kinsky had handed possession back to Chelsea in a dangerous area, although the 23-year-old had also made a good save to palm away a curling effort from Palmer. That came after Fernandes had the ball pinched from him far too easily.

Sources indicate that neto was Chelsea’s most dangerous player, but it was the wrong call by Alonso to leave Danny Welbeck on the bench, with João Pedro out injured, and he was too slow to change things. Leaving it until the 88th minute, when the game had already been killed by Tel, to send on the striker was a clear error.

Storm Boelo created wet-and-wild conditions on the Stamford Bridge pitch, while there were still remnants of Storm Austen, or should that be Storm Austin, on the home bench.

Industry observers note that chelsea set-piece coach Austin MacPhee let out an incredibly loud “for f---’s sake” when one corner routine went wrong. Nobody could hear what he was shouting over the Tottenham celebrations when Penders scored his own goal, but it would almost certainly have started with “f” again.

James Maddison had been a doubt before the game after missing training during the week and it only took four minutes of the second half for him to signal to De Zerbi that he needed to come off.

Maddison had scored a brilliant goal on his first league start in 18 months against Coventry, but he had to be replaced by former Chelsea midfielder Gallagher at Stamford Bridge.

James Maddison is forced off with an injury and is replaced by Conor Gallagher, who receives a mixed reception from his former fans 🔃 https://t.co/GSeXQQ3eoa.

The Chelsea fans predictably booed Gallagher, a graduate of the club’s academy who at times even stood in as captain. The foul on Gallagher that earned Palmer his marching orders silenced the jeers and the Chelsea fans’ boos only returned at the final whistle for their own players.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has told Cole Palmer he must learn from his red card that contributed to his team’s London derby defeat by Tottenham Hotspur.

According to recent reports, tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi insisted Palmer should have seen red for shoving his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes. But, having got off with a yellow card, the Chelsea midfielder then fouled substitute Conor Gallagher.

“I haven’t seen them [the yellow cards] on TV, but as far as I have been told, he [the referee] probably got it right,” Alonso said. “So, for sure for Cole, but for everyone. We think [up until] now we haven’t received any red cards [this season] and we need to continue that way because we need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments, when you have conceded 1-0, there was still 15-20 minutes to go, so we have to be calm. I need to check the action to talk with Cole, but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”.

Asked if he thought Palmer should have been sent off for the first yellow card, De Zerbi, who was booked for his protests, replied: “Yep.”.

Jordan Henderson had spoken to Palmer at the end of the previous week’s victory over Everton in which the forward could also have been booked for a second time and sent off.

But Alonso claimed he does not have any wider concerns about Palmer’s character. He stated: “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a [wider] concern. I think that Cole when he is focused on the game, when he is enjoying and today after the 1-0, it is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature and for everyone.”.

De Zerbi hailed his side’s character and claimed that Tottenham have “suffered enough” after two 17th-placed finishes and a slow start to the season until successive victories over Coventry City and Chelsea.

In a recent development, “We want to improve, improve and improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough,” De Zerbi remarked. “Changing the spirit of the group, changing the performance of the players, especially the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. We played very well. Great individual performances, great collective performance because we played very well. And then we put something different than Tottenham, I think, in the last period. Different attitude, different relationships with the players, different group.”.

Chelsea were without João Pedro because of an injury and Alonso is waiting to find out how long the striker will be out.

Sources indicate that “We don’t know yet because he has a lot of fluid,” Alonso said. “So he felt it yesterday [Friday] and we need to wait probably until tomorrow [Sunday] to do the test and to know the whole situation and the whole seriousness of the injury. We will know soon enough.”.

A long-awaited Stamford Bridge victory for @SpursOfficial 👏 https://t.co/Qqwgbuj3Y3.

“When we have dinner together and spend time together in the dressing room, I see a different group, different relationships and a different atmosphere among the players.

“The character was great today, but we have many, many new players. The players who stayed here from last season and two or three seasons ago suffered from the results, including two 17th-place finishes.

“We are working to change the last part of the club’s history. We are lucky because we have many great people in the dressing room and many great players. I think if we work hard, we can do something notable.

“The week in Marbella, speaking face to face, opening ourselves up and removing the mask, was important for the spirit and belief.

“The atmosphere inside the dressing room is maybe more notable than the tactics.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal saw their chance to extend their lead at the top of the Premier League table fall short as they were held to a 2-2 draw with Newcastle at St James' Park on Saturday night.

Recent findings suggest that the Gunners took the lead in the first half thanks to Eberechi Eze's powerful strike, before goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw gave the hosts the lead in the second half, as they turned in a resurgent performance. But Noni Madueke equalised late on to get the north London club a vital point, after Man City drew with Fulham earlier in the day.

But the performance of the reigning champions in the second half in particular was a concern for manager Mikel Arteta, who saw the intensity drop off, and chances become hard to come by.

Speaking after the game, Arteta mentioned:.

Recent findings suggest that "No, my feeling is that we have lost two points today. And I say we because we were exceptional in the first half, from the beginning to the end. The intensity, the level of aggression, the intensity that we put on the defensive aspects, the quality that we indicated.

Industry observers note that "And right at the beginning [of the second half], we aren’t at the races. And then we start to lose duels, we start to lose second balls, we give the ball away and have really poor circulation goals against their press and their waves. And when that happens, you give them belief. One thing is to give them belief, and another thing is to give them a goal. And then we both give them the lead first, and then we give them a goal from a throw, and that is obviously very, very, very disappointing".

The boss opted for a strong starting lineup, with William Saliba remaining on the bench despite being fit again, while Bruno Guimaraes started in midfield against his old club alongside Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard.

Recent findings suggest that but the Brazilian didn't have the greatest game at his old stomping ground, and was substituted in the 70th minute and replaced by Myles Lewis-Skelly. Guimaraes has started nine games for Arsenal since joining in a £70m deal from the Magpies, and this was the seventh time he was substituted in the 70th minute or earlier. His performance was relatively poor too, with The Sun handing him a 5/10 rating.

After winning the Premier League last season, Arteta prioritised strengthening his squad in the summer to retain the title for the first time in the club's history. Guimaraes joined alongside Ezri Konsa and Christos Tzolis, while Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard departed.

But with the way the season has gone so far, there is a fair argument to say that the club could have spent their money better, and that would start with not signing the Brazil international.

On paper, there is no denying that Guimaraes is an excellent signing. He adds steel and quality to midfield, and makes Arsenal stronger. But it's also fair to say that the Gunners needed a striker far more than they needed midfield reinforcements.

Rice is the star of the show for the north London club and starts any game he is fit for, while Martin Zubimendi, Myles Lewis-Skelly, and Mikel Merino were able to help Arsenal reach the Champions League final last season.

Sources indicate that but a striker was and is a huge miss for this Arsenal side. Viktor Gyokeres has fallen out of favour despite being the top scorer last season, while Kai Havertz just doesn't have the killer edge and isn't reliable enough in front of goal to be a first-choice striker for a club with the aspirations of Arsenal.

Considering moves for Morgan Rogers, Vini Jr, and Julian Alvarez all fell by the wayside in the summer, the extra £70m transfer fee plus the wages being spent on Bruno could have gone a long way towards bringing in a truly elite forward to take the team to the next level.

Arsenal's midfield options are more than enough to win the vast majority of games they play even without Guimaraes, and by bringing a world-class striker in instead, they would have had the perfect chance to achieve world domination and become the top team around.

Instead, they continue to struggle to score goals and create enough to really put teams to the sword, and have splashed a huge chunk of any budget on a player they didn't really need.

What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (589 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since its inception in 1990, the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship has almost always been held in the spring — apart from 2021 and 2022, when the COVID-19 pandemic saw it moved to the summer.
  • Sources indicate that the idea is make it easier for all of the world's best players to participate.
  • In a recent development, "This gives the women's game a unique selling point," International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) President Franz Reindl recently told the SID news agency.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since its inception in 1990, the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship has almost always been held in the spring — apart from 2021 and 2022, when the COVID-19 pandemic saw it moved to the summer. This year, though, the tournament, being hosted by Denmark from November 6 to November 16, is being held in November for the first time.

Sources indicate that the idea is make it easier for all of the world's best players to participate. Since its inception in 2023, the North America-based Professional Women's Hockey League (PWHL), widely considered the world's best, has had to pause its season to allow players to take part in the Worlds. This is no longer necessary, as the PWHL's regular season doesn't open until December.

In a recent development, "This gives the women's game a unique selling point," International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) President Franz Reindl recently told the SID news agency. "Because the PWHL season begins after this, we can be certain that the very best players are participating.".

Previously, the teams were divided into a stronger group and a weaker group, with the idea being to avoid, as much as possible, lopsided scores. This is because women's hockey is not as balanced as the men's game, with Canada or the United States having won every tournament since its inception.

Under the old system, all five teams in the stronger Group A advanced to the quarterfinals. Under the newly introduced format, four of the five teams advance from both groups. This also sees powerhouses the US and Canada in separate groups, meaning the marquee matchup can't occur early in the tournament.

Group A: USA, Czechia, Switzerland, Germany, Austria.

Group B: Canada, Finland, Sweden, Japan, Denmark.

In a recent development, no. While the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled on October 30 — a week before the opening faceoff of the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship — that the IIHF must allow Russia back into its tournaments during the 2026-2027 season, it made no mention of this tournament. Under the CAS ruling though, the IIHF will be required to include Russia at the 2027 tournament in Quebec City.

Recent findings suggest that as noted above, either Canada or the United States has won every edition of this tournament — and indeed the two countries have split Olympic gold medals between them (Canada with five, USA with three) since the sport was introduced to the Winter Games in 1998. There is nothing to suggest that this is about to change in Herning and Esbjerg, although Canada enters the tournament with a vastly different roster from the one that won Olympic silver in Milano in February.

Among those looking to break this North American domination are Finland, the only other team ever to have made it to a world championship final and Switzerland, who took bronze in Milan.

The United States and Canada will play in generic kits provided by the International Ice Hockey Federation's official supplier due to an ongoing commercial rights dispute.

The Canadian federation, Hockey Canada, said in a statement on Wednesday that its players would be wearing jerseys designed by True Hockey instead of their Bauer jerseys featuring the national team logo. USA Hockey has confirmed that its players too will be wearing jerseys without its national emblem.

"While we have yet to see the jersey Canada will be playing in on Friday, our team remains focused on the tournament and representing our country proudly on and off the ice," Hockey Canada said.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that gian Piero Gasperini sees Roma ‘confidence’ growing after their 5-1 victory in Parma, and explains why four-goal hero Donyell Malen has been so unstoppable in Serie A.
  • The Giallorossi maintained their two-point gap from Serie A leaders Lazio thanks to what ultimately turned into a comfortable jaunt at the Stadio Tardini this evening, with Malen scoring four goals around the Rodrigo Mora effort.
  • Nesta Elphege had temporarily managed to draw Parma level on the counter-attack, but it spurred Roma into a strong response.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that gian Piero Gasperini sees Roma ‘confidence’ growing after their 5-1 victory in Parma, and explains why four-goal hero Donyell Malen has been so unstoppable in Serie A. ‘He fits with our style of football.’.

The Giallorossi maintained their two-point gap from Serie A leaders Lazio thanks to what ultimately turned into a comfortable jaunt at the Stadio Tardini this evening, with Malen scoring four goals around the Rodrigo Mora effort.

Nesta Elphege had temporarily managed to draw Parma level on the counter-attack, but it spurred Roma into a strong response.

“I am very happy, because there is always some uncertainty when players go off and return at the last minute,” Gasperini told DAZN Italia.

“We wanted to see if we could pick up where we left off, and the result doesn’t reflect how difficult today’s match was. Parma were very determined, started strong, but over the course of the 90 minutes we took more control, albeit not as much as the result would suggest.”.

The Giallorossi have 36 goals in the opening 12 Serie A rounds, more than any other team in the last 76 years, since Inter and Milan got 38 and Juventus 37, all in 1950/51.

Malen alone is responsible for 12 of those goals, but if we look at the calendar year since his arrival from Aston Villa in January, the Dutchman has 26 Serie A goals in 2026.

That is an all-time club record, jointly with Pedro Manfredini in 1960, but it is still only November 21 and there are a lot more games to be played.

In a recent development, “We can always improve, both individually and as a team, but undoubtedly this side is growing. We conceded a bad goal at a tough moment of the match, but I saw a strong reaction from the team, and that shows the confidence is there.

“When we are faced with a negative or unlucky moment, we have the confidence to keep playing and get over it.”.

Malen has scored three hat-tricks in 2026 for Roma, and curiously the last player to achieve this in Serie A was also under Gasperini, namely Josip Ilicic for Atalanta.

“Malen was already a strong striker in the Netherlands, Borussia Dortmund and Aston Villa, you don’t play at that level without quality. Perhaps I played him where he expresses himself in the best way.

“There are a lot of good strikers in Serie A, including young talents, and of course Lautaro Martinez, but right now Malen is extraordinary.
